# Study MBBS in the Philippines

This site has the details you need before you go: which colleges are on India's NMC list, what the whole five and a half years cost, the documents and the visa, the FMGE after you land back, and what daily life is like in Cebu, Manila and Davao.

[Compare the six colleges](https://drdreams.in/colleges.md)
            [Read the common questions](https://drdreams.in/faq.md)

Every page carries the date it was last checked. The record behind the advice, and how to correct a page, is on [the about page](https://drdreams.in/about.md).

November 2026: the Philippine licence is now open

Indian graduates of recognised Philippine medical schools can now sit the Physician Licensure Examination and register to practise in the Philippines, after the Philippine Professional Regulation Commission cleared the reciprocity rule. The Embassy of India, Manila confirmed it. It does not replace FMGE or NExT for practising in India. [What changed, and what it does not](https://drdreams.in/ple-philippines.md).

Most students begin with a college name someone mentioned. The useful order is the other way round: check the recognition, then the money, then the life. Each one has a page.

1.

### Is this college on India's NMC list?

If it is not, the degree will not get you registered in India. It takes about two minutes to check, and the method is on the page. [See the six colleges](https://drdreams.in/colleges.md), or read the [2026 NMC rules](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules.md) first.

2.

### What do the whole five and a half years cost?

Tuition is the number everyone quotes. Tuition plus hostel plus food plus flights plus the visa renewal is the number that empties the account. [The full cost breakdown](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md).

3.

### What does an ordinary week look like?

Food, weather, safety, the accent in lectures, how far the hospital is. This is what students ask at month three. [Life in the Philippines](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md).

Passport, marksheets, NEET scorecard, birth certificate, police clearance, medical certificate, bank statement. Each one has a format and an authentication step, and the whole list is shorter than the panic around it suggests.

[See the document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md)
          [The process, step by step](https://drdreams.in/admission-process.md)

The honest version

## What the degree gives you, and what it does not

An MD from a listed Philippine college is recognised in India. That is the whole promise, and it holds only while the college stays on the list. What it does not do is make you a doctor in India on graduation day.

You still sit FMGE or NExT, and you still complete a year of internship in India before you can register. Students who treat that as a formality are the ones who end up repeating the exam. Students who start studying for it in first year clear it.

The clinical training here is genuinely good. Philippine hospitals are busy, and foreign students are allowed hands on patients, which is not true everywhere. That is the part worth paying for.

Cebu. Five and a half years of it, and the beach is not the reason to go, but it is not nothing.

The mechanics

## From shortlist to a seat in class

Five steps, in order. The full version, with the document list and the visa paperwork, is on the process page.

1.

### Check the college, then email it

Confirm the college on the NMC and WDOMS lists, then write to its international admissions office from the contact on the college's own website.

2.

### Send documents and get the acceptance letter

Marksheets, passport, birth certificate, photographs. The letter is what the embassy and the airline will ask for.

3.

### Apply for the student visa

The college issues a support letter. The embassy handles the rest. This is the one stage where paying a visa consultant is reasonable.

4.

### Book the flight and the first month of housing

Book direct. Reserve a hostel through the student affairs office before you land, then look at apartments once you know the city.

5.

### Arrive, register, and start the long part

Airport pickup, enrolment, and the first month of figuring out where to eat. The [student life page](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md) covers that month.

[Full process and document list](https://drdreams.in/admission-process.md)

Questions

## The three that decide everything else

Is an MD from the Philippines valid in India?

Only if the college is on India's NMC list when you enrol and when you graduate. After the MD you sit FMGE or NExT and complete a year of internship in India before you can register to practise.

Check the college on the NMC and WDOMS lists yourself before you pay anything. [What the exams involve](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next.md).

Can I study medicine in the Philippines without clearing NEET?

There is a route through a pre-medical BSBio year, but NEET still has to be cleared before the MD, because NMC requires it for Indian students who want to practise in India. The BSBio year buys time to prepare. It does not replace the exam.

[How the BSBio route actually works](https://drdreams.in/without-neet.md).

What documents do I need to apply?

Class 10 and 12 marksheets, your NEET scorecard, passport with at least eighteen months of validity, birth certificate, a medical certificate, police clearance and proof of funds. Most colleges also ask for passport photographs and a short personal statement.

[The full checklist, with formats and authentication](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md).

Guide

# MBBS in the Philippines: complete guide for Indian students

What the degree is, who recognises it, what it costs, and how the six years pass. Written for a student and a parent reading the same page, and updated when the rules move.

Last reviewed November 2026.

## On this page

1. Why students choose it

2. The degree, and how long it takes

3. Recognition in India

4. The six colleges

5. What it costs

6. NEET and the BSBio year

7. Getting in

8. What the week looks like

9. The four expensive mistakes

10. A timeline for the 2027 intake

## 1. Why students choose it

There are four honest reasons, and one bad one.

The first is language. Lectures, textbooks, hospital charts and patients are all in English. In Russia or China you spend the first years learning a language just to understand a ward round. Here you start as a medical student on day one.

The second is clinical access. Philippine hospitals are busy, and students are allowed to examine patients, assist in deliveries and stand in theatre from the clinical years. In several other destinations foreign students watch. Watching is not the same as doing, and the difference shows up when you sit an exam that tests clinical judgement.

The third is the shape of the degree. It follows the American model: a four-year MD after a bachelor's, with the internship built into the programme. You graduate with a Doctor of Medicine, which NMC treats as equivalent to MBBS for Indian registration.

The fourth is distance and culture. Flights from India run five to six hours, the climate is tropical, and Filipino families are warm to Indian students in a way that makes the first year survivable. Cebu in particular feels less like a foreign country than like a very different Indian city.

The bad reason is that it looks cheap in a brochure. It is cheaper than a private Indian medical seat. It is not cheap, and it is not a shortcut. Treat it as a long, expensive, serious course of study that happens to be abroad.

## 2. The degree, and how long it takes

You graduate with a **Doctor of Medicine (MD)**. In the Philippines that is the primary medical degree, not a postgraduate one. NMC recognises it as equivalent to MBBS for the purpose of Indian registration, provided the college is on the list.

The programme runs about **five and a half years including internship**. The first two years are classroom and laboratory: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, then pathology, pharmacology, microbiology and the rest. Third year onwards you are in the hospital. The final year is a rotating internship.

If you take the BSBio pre-medical year first, add six months to a year. That route exists mainly for students who still need to clear NEET, and [it has its own page](https://drdreams.in/without-neet.md).

One warning about duration. Curricula change, and NMC's requirements have tightened. A college that quotes you four years is either describing an old programme or a compressed one that will cause you problems at registration. Ask for the current curriculum in writing.

## 3. Recognition in India

This is the section to read twice.

Your degree is useful in India if, and only if, the college appears on the National Medical Commission's list of recognised foreign medical institutions. Not "will be listed soon". Not "in process". On the list, when you enrol, and when you graduate.

Check two places before you pay anything:

- The NMC's own list, at [nmc.org.in](https://www.nmc.org.in).

- The World Directory of Medical Schools, at [search.wdoms.org](https://search.wdoms.org). NMC's 2026 notice leans on this directory for verification.

Then there is the part nobody puts in the brochure. After the MD, you sit **FMGE**, which is being replaced by **NExT** over time, and you complete a **twelve month internship in India** before you register with a state medical council. The exam is hard, and the students who fail are usually the ones who planned to start preparing after graduation. [More on both exams](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next.md).

The 2026 rules added detail on the 54 month requirement, compensation for any online teaching, and internship verification. [The full notice, with the official PDF](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules.md), is worth an hour of your time before you commit.

## 4. The six colleges

Six are covered here: one studied at, three visited, and all six known through graduates worth trusting. Three sit in Cebu, one in Metro Manila, two in Davao. They differ in cost, in batch size, in hospital size, and in whether FMGE coaching happens on campus.

| College | City | Best for | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**GCM Gullas**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md) | Cebu | Lowest entry cost, on-campus FMGE coaching | Large batch, basic hostel |
| [**Southwestern**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/southwestern.md) | Cebu | Hospital rotations, smaller Indian batch | No in-house FMGE coaching |
| [**Perpetual Help**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/perpetual.md) | Las Piñas | Indian community, food, coaching | Manila traffic, higher living cost |
| [**DMSF**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/dmsf.md) | Davao | Clinical volume, anatomy lab | Higher fees, longer flight home |
| [**Brokenshire**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/brokenshire.md) | Davao | Small batches, faculty attention | Smaller attached hospital |
| [**Jose Maria**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/jmc.md) | Davao | Tightest budget, medical missions | Cook for yourself, basic facilities |

The six colleges, in the order we would shortlist them for a typical budget.

[The comparison page](https://drdreams.in/colleges.md) has fees, food, batch size and the rating side by side.

## 5. What it costs

For the whole programme, tuition plus hostel plus food plus flights plus visa renewals, most families land between **Rs 15 lakh and Rs 25 lakh**. The spread comes from the college, the city, and whether you cook or eat out.

A private Indian medical seat, by comparison, is quoted in tens of lakhs for tuition alone, before donation. That gap is why this option exists at all. It is not a small amount of money, and a quote that presents it as cheap is worth checking line by line.

The [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md) breaks the total into each component and compares it with Russia, Georgia, China and Kazakhstan.

## 6. NEET and the BSBio year

NMC requires NEET for Indian students who intend to practise in India. That is the rule, and nothing waives it.

What exists is a workaround in timing, not in requirement. You enrol in BSBio, a pre-medical biology year at a Philippine university, without NEET. While you study, you prepare for and sit NEET. Once you clear it, you move into the MD at the same university. You lose six months to a year, and you gain a year of English-medium science teaching and a soft landing in a new country.

Students who have already done a year of serious NEET coaching usually skip BSBio and go straight to the MD, provided their NEET score qualifies them. [The detailed version is here](https://drdreams.in/without-neet.md), including what BSBio does and does not fix.

## 7. Getting in

The short version: pick the college, email its international office, send documents, get the acceptance letter, apply for the visa, fly. There is no entrance exam of the kind you are imagining, and there is no lottery.

The documents are ones you already have or can obtain in a week: 10th and 12th marksheets, passport, birth certificate, police clearance, medical fitness certificate, photographs. The [process page](https://drdreams.in/admission-process.md) lists them with the order of operations and the visa steps.

The process is mostly email and patience. The one stage where paying someone is reasonable is the visa file, if your documents are messy or you have a refusal on record, because a rejected application costs a semester.

## 8. What the week looks like

Classes in the morning, lab or ward in the afternoon, and then the real work: figuring out dinner. Food is the thing every Indian student underestimates. Cebu has Indian restaurants and spice shops, but not on every corner. Learn to cook three things before you leave.

The accent takes about a month to tune into. The heat takes about a week. The loneliness takes longer, and it is the reason to pick a college with a decent Indian batch if you are the kind of person who needs company. [Food, safety, housing and money, in detail](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md).

## 9. The four expensive mistakes

- **Paying a deposit before checking the college.** Check the NMC list first. It takes two minutes and it is free.

- **Choosing on first-year fees alone.** A cheap first year with expensive later years is a sales technique, not a discount.

- **Starting FMGE preparation in the final year.** By then the subjects you need are two years behind you. Start in first year, slowly.

- **Believing the college will handle your registration.** The college handles its paperwork. Yours is yours, and NMC's verification is strict about the internship and the 54 month requirement.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md), and how to check a fee quote.

## 10. A timeline for the 2027 intake

Months move between colleges, so treat this as a shape rather than a schedule, and confirm dates with the admissions office.

1. **Now to February.** Shortlist two or three colleges. Check each on the NMC and WDOMS lists. Get the current fee sheet from each in writing.

2. **February to April.** Prepare documents. Sit NEET if you have not. Speak to students in your shortlisted colleges before you choose.

3. **April to June.** Apply. Receive the acceptance letter. Start the visa file.

4. **June to August.** Visa, flight, hostel reservation, first month of money in a Philippine bank account once you land.

5. **August onwards.** Enrolment and the first semester. Join or form a study group early, because the FMGE clock starts now, not in year four.

The one line version

Pick a college that is on the NMC list, confirm the total cost in writing, learn to cook, and start FMGE preparation in first year. Everything else is detail, and the detail is on the pages linked above.

Questions

## What families ask before they commit

How long does MBBS take in the Philippines?

About five and a half years including internship. Add six months to a year if you take the BSBio pre-medical route. Confirm the current curriculum with the college in writing, because it has changed before.

Is NEET required to study medicine in the Philippines?

NMC requires NEET for Indian students who intend to practise in India. Some colleges admit students to BSBio without it, and the student clears NEET before the MD. Going without NEET and expecting to practise in India is the mistake, not the BSBio year.

Is the Philippines better than Russia or China?

The teaching is in English, patients speak English, and foreign students get hands on clinical work, which is not true in every destination. The trade off is cost and distance from home. Whether it is better depends on your budget and how you handle being far away, not on a ranking.

What happens after the MD?

You sit FMGE or NExT, complete a twelve month internship in India, then register with the state medical council. Plan for that exam from the first year, not the last. [Both exams explained](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next.md).

## The next page to read

Cost is the part families underestimate, and the part most quotes are vague about. The numbers, line by line, are on the next page.

### Short answers, if you are in a hurry

- It takes five and a half years and costs Rs 15 to 25 lakh.

- The college must be on the NMC list, checked by you, on the day you enrol.

- NEET is required to practise in India. The BS Biology year does not replace it.

- The teaching is in English. Life in Cebu and Davao is cheaper than Manila.

- After the MD you come home, clear FMGE or NExT, and do a year of internship.

## What is MBBS in the Philippines called?

The degree is a Doctor of Medicine, or MD. It is the Philippine equivalent of the Indian MBBS and it is what Indian students mean when they say MBBS in the Philippines. Filipino colleges also run a separate four-year pre-medical bachelor's degree, usually BS Biology, which their own students take before the MD.

The MD runs five and a half years including the internship, is taught in English, and is open to foreign students who have finished class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology. On paper it is a postgraduate degree. In practice, for an Indian student arriving after class 12, it is a single continuous programme from first year to internship. [The full guide to the degree](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines.md).

## How long does MBBS take in the Philippines?

Five and a half years: four years of classroom and clinical study, then a twelve-month internship in a hospital attached to the same university. Students who take the BS Biology year first add another year.

NMC's Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations require the foreign course to run at least 54 months of academic study, excluding internship, and the internship to be completed at the same institution. A 5.5-year MD satisfies both if you finish on time. The whole thing has to be completed within ten years of joining, including any repeated year, so a lost year is survivable but not free. [What the 2026 notice changed](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules.md).

## What does MBBS in the Philippines cost?

Between Rs 15 lakh and Rs 25 lakh for the whole programme, for most students at the six colleges on this site. Tuition alone is the smaller half of that number.

The rest is hostel, food, flights twice a year, visa renewals, health insurance, FMGE coaching where it is not included, and a buffer for the emergency nobody plans for. The cheapest college and the most expensive one differ by about ten lakh over five and a half years. That is a real gap, but it is smaller than most quotes suggest, because flights and living costs are the same wherever you go. [Line by line, with a worksheet](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md).

## Is MBBS from the Philippines valid in India?

Yes, if the college is on India's NMC list when you enrol and when you graduate, and if you clear FMGE or NExT and then complete a twelve-month internship in India. Skip any of those and the degree will not get you registered to practise.

The NMC list is the whole test. A college that is not on it produces a degree India will not recognise, whatever a brochure says. Check the list yourself on the NMC site and cross-check the college on WDOMS, then keep the screenshot with the date on it. [The six colleges, with their NMC status](https://drdreams.in/colleges.md).

## What are the latest NMC rules for Philippines graduates?

The rules that matter are the Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations 2021 and the NMC public notice of 5 March 2026. Together they require a course of at least 54 months, a twelve-month internship at the same foreign university, WDOMS listing, and a twelve-month compulsory rotating internship in India after you clear FMGE or NExT.

The body was called the Medical Council of India, or MCI, until 2020, so older posts still say MCI rules for the Philippines. The rules now come from the NMC. The body was called the Medical Council of India, or MCI, until 2020, so older posts still say MCI rules for the Philippines; the rules now come from the NMC. If you joined before 18 November 2021, the older Screening Test Regulations apply to you. If you joined on or after that date, the 2021 regulations apply in full. The 2026 notice tightened verification rather than banning anyone, and it is the reason you should keep every admit card, fee receipt and attendance record from your college. [The notice, explained with the official PDF](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules.md).

## Can I study MBBS in the Philippines without NEET?

You can start, but you cannot finish and practise in India without it. Some colleges admit students to the BS Biology year without NEET, and the student clears NEET before moving into the MD. NMC requires NEET for Indian students who want to practise in India, with no exceptions.

The BS Biology route is useful for a student who missed the exam or scored too low for a seat, and it costs an extra year and about three to four lakh rupees. It buys time to prepare. It does not replace the exam. [How the BS Biology route works](https://drdreams.in/without-neet.md).

## Which colleges in the Philippines are taking admissions for 2027?

All six colleges covered here are accepting applications for the 2027 intake. Philippine medical colleges run one main intake a year, with classes beginning in August and September, and applications stay open through the spring until seats fill.

The practical deadline is not the application form. It is the visa appointment and the document authentication, both of which take weeks. A student who applies in June for an August start is usually too late. February to May is the working window. [Compare the six, including fees and hospital size](https://drdreams.in/colleges.md).

## What documents do I need to apply?

Class 10 and 12 marksheets, NEET scorecard, passport with eighteen months of validity, birth certificate, medical certificate, police clearance, passport photographs, proof of funds, and the college's application form with a short personal statement.

The birth certificate and marksheets usually need notarisation, state attestation and a Ministry of External Affairs apostille before the embassy will accept them, which takes two to four weeks. [The full checklist with formats](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md).

## Is it safe to study MBBS in the Philippines?

For a student living in a hostel near campus, in Cebu, Manila or Davao, yes. The bigger risks are traffic, petty theft and bad decisions at two in the morning, not violence against foreign students. Thousands of Indian students have lived there for years without incident.

Practical rules that actually keep you safe: live within walking distance of campus or on a well-lit main road, use Grab instead of unlicensed taxis at night, do not carry a laptop in a backpack on a jeepney, keep your documents in a hostel safe, and tell someone where you are going. The cities are not dangerous in the way the news makes them sound. They are not so safe that you can be careless, either. [What daily life is actually like](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md).

## Is the course taught in English?

Yes. Lectures, textbooks, examinations and hospital records are in English, and English is one of the two official languages of the Philippines. Filipino and Bisaya are spoken in corridors and canteens.

The first month is hard anyway. Professors speak English with a Filipino accent, patients mix in Bisaya, and the speed takes getting used to. Most students understand two thirds of the first lectures and everything by the end of the first semester. Nobody fails for the accent. [More on the language problem](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md).

## Do I need to learn Filipino or Bisaya?

No. You can complete the degree in English. Learning a hundred words of Bisaya or Tagalog will change your hospital experience, though, and patients will treat you differently for trying.

Clinical years are where it matters. A patient who understands your question answers it. A patient who does not gives you a nod and a guess. Ordering food, asking directions and haggling in the market are the other places a little language goes a long way.

## Is FMGE compulsory after I come back?

Yes, if you want to practise in India. Foreign medical graduates sit FMGE or, once it is fully in place, NExT, then complete a twelve-month internship in India, then register with a state medical council.

The pass rate is low, in the range of one in five to one in four in most sessions. Most of that is timing: students start preparing in final year. The ones who clear it begin in first year, with Indian textbooks alongside the Philippine ones. [A study plan by year](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next.md).

## Can I work in the Philippines after graduating?

Yes, since November 2026. The Philippine Professional Regulation Commission now permits Indian graduates of recognised Philippine medical schools to sit the Physician Licensure Examination (PLE) and register to practise in the country. The Embassy of India in Manila confirmed the change. Before this, Philippine law required India to give Filipino doctors the same right, and it did not, so the route was closed.

The PLE gives you a licence to practise in the Philippines. It does not register you in India: to work here you still sit FMGE or NExT and complete the twelve month internship, whichever route you take. If you want to stay, prepare for the PLE the way you prepare for FMGE, from first year. Confirm the current eligibility with the Professional Regulation Commission and your college before you rely on it. [How the Philippine licence works](https://drdreams.in/ple-philippines.md).

## What is the difference between MD in the Philippines and MBBS in India?

On paper, the Philippine MD is a postgraduate degree and the Indian MBBS is an undergraduate one. In practice both are five and a half years with an internship, both are taught in English, and both lead to a licence only after a qualifying exam and internship in the country where you want to work.

The real differences are clinical and cultural. Philippine hospitals let students do hands-on work early, which Indian colleges often do not. The trade is that you do your internship in the Philippines and then repeat a year of internship in India after FMGE, so the whole path is longer than the Indian one by about a year. [The complete comparison](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines.md).

## How much does living in the Philippines cost per month?

Less than most Indian cities for rent, more for groceries. A shared or hostel room, food, transport, phone data and the occasional night out come to a modest monthly figure, and the hostel is where students either save or overspend.

In Cebu and Davao a basic hostel is cheap and a comfortable one is not. Manila costs more for everything except food, and the traffic costs you time you will not get back. Cooking for yourself is the single biggest saving, and the reason a college with an Indian mess works out cheaper than its tuition suggests. [The full cost breakdown](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md).

## When should I start applying for the 2027 intake?

Start in December or January for an August 2027 start. By February you should know your shortlist, by March you should have the college's conditional acceptance, and by May your visa file should be at the embassy.

The order that works: check NMC and WDOMS first, email the colleges, get the document list in writing, start authentication while you wait, sit NEET if you have not, then apply for the visa as soon as the acceptance letter arrives. Every year a batch of students misses the intake because they began in June. [The step-by-step timeline](https://drdreams.in/admission-process.md).

## Can my parents visit me during the course?

Yes. They can apply for a visitor visa, and most colleges will issue an invitation letter if the admissions office is asked in advance. Flights are cheapest booked two to three months out, and December and January are the expensive weeks.

A visit in the first semester is worth more than it sounds. Parents who have seen the hostel, met the warden and eaten in the mess stop worrying, and students who are not managing a worried phone call every night do better in first year.

## What happens if I fail a subject or lose a year?

You repeat the subject, usually in a summer term or with the next batch, and you pay for the repeat. The degree does not disappear. What you cannot do is stretch the whole programme past ten years from the date you joined, because NMC will not recognise a course that took longer.

One repeated subject is common and recoverable. Three lost years is a different problem. If you are failing, the fix is almost always the same: fewer hours in the hostel, more hours in the library, and an honest conversation with the faculty before the exam rather than after it.

## Where to go next

If your question is not on this page, send it. Questions that keep coming up get added here with the answer.

[Read the full guide](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines.md)
          [Ask a question](https://drdreams.in/contact.md)

Money

# MBBS in the Philippines fees: what five years really cost

Tuition is the number every college quotes first, and the only number that is easy to compare. The bill that empties an account is tuition plus eight other lines. This page lists all of them, and gives you a worksheet to fill from your own quotes.

Reviewed November 2026. Ranges are indicative, based on years spent there and what students reported. Always use a current fee sheet from the college.

## The two numbers

Typical total, whole programme

Rs 15 to 25 lakh

What changes it most

College and city

Second biggest factor

Whether you cook

Hidden lines

Six, listed below

Cheapest first year

Not the cheapest degree

Why the published sheets live on the college pages

Four of the six colleges have published 2026-2027 fee sheets, and they are on each college page and summarised below. Sheets change every intake, sometimes twice a year, so treat them as a starting point and confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay.

What this page can do is tell you exactly which lines to ask for, and how they add up. That is worth more than a number that ages badly.

The lines

## Eight things you will pay for

Ask for each of these separately, in writing, from the college. A quote that cannot be broken into these lines is either disorganised or hiding something.

1.

### Tuition, per year

The biggest line, and the one that rises. Ask for the fee for each year of the programme, not just year one. Some colleges hold it flat, some do not.

2.

### Hostel

Per month or per semester. Confirm whether air conditioning, electricity and water are included. In Cebu and Davao, a basic hostel is cheap; a comfortable one is not.

3.

### Food

An Indian mess is the cheapest option where one exists. Where it does not, you are cooking, and groceries in the Philippines are not as cheap as in India. This line is where the cheapest college turns expensive.

4.

### Flights, twice a year

Manila and Cebu are easier and cheaper to reach than Davao. Multiply by five years. It is a real line, not a rounding error.

5.

### Visa and immigration costs

The student visa, then renewals, then the annual registration with Philippine immigration. These recur every year and are almost never in the quote you get in India.

6.

### Health insurance

Usually required, usually annual, and often forgotten until enrolment week.

7.

### FMGE coaching

Included at some colleges, separate at others, and not offered at all at one. If it is separate, price an online Indian course before you choose, because you will need one.

8.

### A buffer

One emergency flight home, one medical bill, one laptop replacement. Every batch has a student who needed it. Put it in the budget from the start.

Worksheet

## Build your own total

Print this, or copy it into a notebook. Fill the middle column from the college's written quote and the right column from your own estimate. If the two totals differ by more than you are comfortable with, you have found the gap before it hurts.

| Line | College quote | Your estimate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tuition, all years |  |  |
| Hostel, all years |  |  |
| Food, all years |  |  |
| Flights, twice a year |  |  |
| Visa and renewals |  |  |
| Health insurance |  |  |
| FMGE coaching |  |  |
| Buffer |  |  |
| **Total** |  |  |

Five-year total worksheet. Leave a row blank if it does not apply.

An empty cell is still a number you will pay. Write zero only when the college has confirmed zero in writing.

Published sheets

## Fee sheets published for the 2026-2027 intake

Four of the six colleges have published fee sheets for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges are already quoted in rupees. Southwestern and Perpetual publish theirs on request.

| Component | Gullas | DMSF | Jose Maria | Brokenshire |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enrolment fee | Rs 2,25,000 | Rs 2,50,000 | Rs 2,25,000 | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,25,000 | Rs 2,50,000 | Rs 2,25,000 | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,25,000 | Rs 2,50,000 | Rs 2,25,000 | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing | Rs 1,50,000 | Rs 1,50,000 | Rs 1,50,000 | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Book or uniform fee | Rs 40,000 | Rs 40,000 | Rs 40,000 | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | 1,25,000 PHP (Rs 1,80,966) | USD 2,750 (Rs 2,54,871) | 1,20,000 PHP (Rs 1,73,727) | 1,10,000 PHP (Rs 1,59,250) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 14,000 PHP (Rs 20,268) | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) |
| FMGE coaching campus | Gullas and KINGS | DMSF and KINGS | JMCM and KINGS (Chennai) | Brokenshire and KINGS |

Side by side, 2026-2027 published sheets. Scroll sideways on a phone.

Full per-college detail, including the facilities list and the bundled services, is on each college page: [Gullas](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md), [DMSF](https://drdreams.in/colleges/dmsf.md), [Jose Maria](https://drdreams.in/colleges/jmc.md), [Brokenshire](https://drdreams.in/colleges/brokenshire.md).

The enrolment fee is not refunded at any of the four. Visa conversion and extension in the Philippines are paid by the student at actual cost. The internship fee is discussed at the time of internship at DMSF, Jose Maria and Brokenshire.

Comparison

## Against the other destinations

These are the ranges quoted to students we have spoken to, and what students from those countries reported. Treat them as a starting point for your own calls, not as prices.

| Destination | Typically quoted | Language of teaching | The real difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Philippines** | Rs 15 to 25 lakh | English | Clinical access for foreign students, tropical climate, 5 to 6 hour flight |
| Russia | Rs 20 to 35 lakh | Russian in the early years | Cold winters, limited patient contact for foreign students |
| Georgia | Rs 25 to 40 lakh | English, heavy accent | High cost, small Indian community, cold winters |
| China | Rs 20 to 30 lakh | Mandarin by the clinical years | Language barrier in hospitals, very different food culture |
| Kazakhstan | Rs 18 to 25 lakh | Russian and Kazakh | Fewer Indian students, little FMGE coaching infrastructure |
| Ukraine | Not recommended now | Ukrainian and Russian | Ongoing conflict. Students have had to leave mid-course |

Indicative ranges and the practical differences, not a price list.

The point of the table is not that the Philippines wins. It is that the cheapest headline is rarely the cheapest degree, and the language of instruction changes your entire clinical training. A destination where you cannot speak to a patient is not cheaper, it is a different course.

Worth paying for

## Where money is well spent

- **A visa consultant, if the file is messy.** One rejection costs a semester. A licensed consultant who has processed Philippine student visas before earns the fee in that one case.

- **A good hostel in year one.** Security and a short commute matter more than saving two thousand pesos a month.

- **An FMGE course from first year.** The cheapest insurance you will ever buy against repeating an exam.

- **Health insurance.** Non-negotiable. One hospital admission without it can cost more than a year of premiums.

Not worth paying for

## Where money disappears

- **Cash paid without a receipt.** Fees go to the institution and come back on college letterhead. If the receipt is a handwritten note, it is not a receipt.

- **"Documentation charges" on top of a quote.** Photocopies and couriers cost a few hundred rupees. Anything larger needs an itemised bill.

- **Deposits paid before an acceptance letter exists.** The letter is the only thing that proves a seat. Pay after it, not before it.

- **Two quotes that do not match.** Ask both for the same eight lines. The gap between them is the part nobody explained.

Before any transfer

No college in the Philippines needs money sent to an individual's personal account. Fees go to the institution, and you get a receipt on college letterhead. If the account name is a person, stop and ask why in writing.

The [document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) covers what the money is buying at each stage.

Questions

## The money questions, answered plainly

What is the total cost of MBBS in the Philippines?

Most families spend between roughly Rs 15 lakh and Rs 25 lakh across the whole programme, including tuition, hostel, food, flights and visa renewals. The spread comes from the college, the city and whether the student cooks.

Ask each college for a current fee sheet rather than relying on any published figure, including this one.

Is it cheaper than a private medical college in India?

The tuition is lower than a private Indian medical seat, which is often quoted in tens of lakhs before any donation. It is not cheap in absolute terms, and the living costs of five and a half years abroad are real. Compare the all-in total, not the first-year fee.

What costs get left out of a fee quote?

Visa renewals, the annual registration with Philippine immigration, health insurance, hostel deposits, local fees payable in pesos, flights home, and FMGE coaching. Those six lines are where a quote that looked affordable turns into a budget problem in year two.

## Ask for the fee sheet

Every college has a fee sheet for the intake. Ask for it in writing, with hostel and miscellaneous lines included. If someone quotes a single total instead, ask which lines it covers.

[The document list](https://drdreams.in/admission-process.md)

title: "MBBS in the Philippines Without NEET: How the BSBio Route Works"
description: "The honest version of studying medicine in the Philippines without clearing NEET: what BSBio does, how long it adds, what NMC actually requires, and the risks."

No NEET score

# MBBS in the Philippines without NEET

There is a route. It does not skip the exam. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you a problem you will meet again in year five, in a room in India, with an NMC officer asking for your NEET result.

Reviewed November 2026. Rules change, so check the current NMC position before you commit money.

Read this first

NMC requires NEET for Indian students who want to practise in India. That requirement sits on the student, not on the college. A Philippine college can admit you to a pre-medical course without NEET. It cannot make you eligible for Indian registration without it.

So the honest framing is this: you are not choosing between NEET and no NEET. You are choosing where and when you sit it.

The route

## What BSBio actually is

BSBio is Bachelor of Science in Biology, a normal undergraduate science degree in the Philippines. It is a pre-medical course, six months to a year of it depending on how the college structures the transfer, and it exists in Philippine universities independently of any Indian student. It is not a medical degree, and it is not a back door.

The arrangement Indian students use is straightforward. You enrol in BSBio, which does not require NEET. While you study, you prepare for and sit NEET. When you clear it, the same university moves you into the MD programme. You have spent the year in an English-medium science classroom, in the city you are going to live in, with the paperwork for your student visa already done.

What it does not do is reduce the MD by a year. The MD is still about five and a half years. Add the BSBio year and you are looking at six to six and a half years abroad, plus the FMGE and the Indian internship afterwards.

Check the bachelor's degree itself

The Philippine Doctor of Medicine is a postgraduate course, and enrolment needs a bachelor's degree and the NMAT. The Embassy of India, Manila is clear that the pre-medical degree must itself be accredited by CHED, that its content must meet the MD eligibility requirements, and that its duration must follow CHED's guidelines. Ask the college to put all three in writing before you enrol in BSBio.

## BSBio compared with the other pre-med courses

Philippine universities run several pre-medical degrees, and Indian students ask which one is best. The honest answer is that only two routes matter for you: the BSBio bridging year, or direct entry to the MD after class 12. The four-year degrees below are for Filipino students who are still deciding on a career.

| Route | Time before the MD | What it gives you | Worth it for an Indian student? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **BS Biology (bridging year)** | 6 to 12 months | Biology and chemistry in English, at the university that will take you into the MD | Yes, if you need a year to clear NEET. It is the route most colleges use for the transfer. |
| **BS Medical Technology** | 4 years plus a board exam | Laboratory and diagnostics training | Rarely. It adds four years and still leaves you doing the full MD. |
| **BS Nursing** | 4 years plus a licence | Ward experience and patient handling | No. It is a separate career, not a shortcut into medicine. |
| **BS Pharmacy** | 4 years plus a licence | Pharmacology and dispensing | No. Useful knowledge, wrong length for this decision. |
| **BS Psychology** | 4 years | Behavioural science, lighter on the hard sciences | No. The weakest preparation for the MD of the five. |
| **Direct MD entry** | None | The full five and a half years, starting now | Yes, if your class 12 marks are strong and NEET is already done. It is the fastest route. |

Pre-medical routes, and what each one does for an Indian student

One thing none of these do is shorten the medical course. NMC counts the 54 months of the MD and the twelve-month internship, not the year before it. A four-year pre-med degree does not buy you a shorter MD, and it does not exempt you from FMGE.

## Who the BSBio year genuinely helps

- **Students who missed NEET by a margin they can close.** A year of structured biology in English, with fewer distractions, is a real second attempt with better conditions.

- **Students who need to be somewhere else to focus.** Some people cannot study at home. It helps to admit that, and it says nothing bad about you.

- **Families who want the landing spread out.** Arriving a year before the MD starts means the culture shock, the cooking, the accent and the homesickness happen outside the hardest academic year.

## Who it does not help

- **Students who did not study at all.** A new country does not fix a study habit. It removes the support that was hiding the problem.

- **Anyone told they can skip NEET entirely.** They cannot, and whoever told them knows it.

- **Anyone on a tight budget.** The extra year costs an extra year: tuition, hostel, food, flights, visa renewal. It is the single most expensive way to prepare for an exam you could have prepared for at home.

Step by step

## The sequence, and where it goes wrong

1.

### Confirm the college offers BSBio and a transfer

Not every college on this site runs the route. Ask for the transfer arrangement in writing: the conditions, the timeline, and whether a seat in the MD is held or merely hoped for.

2.

### Apply to BSBio

12th marksheet, passport, birth certificate, photographs. No NEET result is required for this step. [The document list](https://drdreams.in/admission-process.md) is the same one you will use later.

3.

### Get the acceptance letter and the visa

The letter names the course. Keep it. You will need it again at the embassy, at immigration, and at enrolment.

4.

### Study BSBio and prepare for NEET in parallel

This is the year. Two to three hours a day of NEET preparation on top of classes is the realistic load. The biology overlaps, which helps, but the chemistry and physics do not teach themselves.

5.

### Sit NEET and clear it

Register as a private candidate, travel if you must, and sit the exam. This is the step that decides whether the year was a detour or a dead end.

6.

### Transfer into the MD

Get the transfer in writing, with the date. Do not rely on a verbal assurance from an admissions clerk three months before the semester starts.

Where it goes wrong

The common failure is not the exam. It is the transfer. Students arrive on a BSBio acceptance letter with a verbal promise of an MD seat, then discover the MD intake is full, or the credits do not transfer the way they were told, or the college has changed the arrangement. Get every one of those in writing before you pay.

The alternative

## If you already did a year of NEET coaching

Students who have already spent a year in serious NEET coaching usually do not need BSBio. If your score qualifies you, you go straight into the MD. The coaching year already did the job BSBio would do, and you save a year of fees and a year of your life.

Talk to the college about its current entry requirements for the MD directly. Requirements have changed before and will change again, and the only version that counts is the one the college confirms in writing for your intake. The [NMC rules page](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules.md) tracks the regulatory side, with the official notice and PDF.

## What it costs, roughly

A BSBio year is cheaper than an MD year, but it is not free: tuition, hostel, food, flights and a visa renewal. Add it to your five-year total before you decide. The [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md) has a worksheet for exactly this.

## The straight answer

If you can clear NEET at home with one more year of preparation, that is cheaper and faster than doing it in Cebu. The BSBio route makes sense when the year abroad is genuinely better for you than the year at home, not when it is a way to avoid the exam.

Questions

## What students ask about this route

Can I study MBBS in the Philippines without NEET?

You can enrol in the BSBio pre-medical year without NEET at colleges that offer it. You cannot qualify to practise in India without clearing NEET, because NMC requires it for Indian students. The BSBio year buys preparation time, not an exemption.

How long does the BSBio route add?

Six months to a year, depending on the college and when you clear NEET and transfer. The MD itself remains about five and a half years including internship.

Is the BSBio route legal and safe?

BSBio is a normal Philippine pre-medical degree and many Indian students take it. The risk is not the course, it is the promise around it. Confirm with the college in writing that your BSBio year transitions into their MD, and confirm NMC's current requirements before you pay.

## The exam is still the plan

The biology year buys time. It does not buy a licence, and NEET still has to be cleared. The FMGE page explains the exam that comes after the degree.

[FMGE and NExT](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next.md)
          [The admission process](https://drdreams.in/admission-process.md)

The mechanics

# Philippines student visa and admission process

The whole process, in the order it happens, with the documents you actually need. Most of it is paperwork you can do yourself in a fortnight. The visa is the part worth paying attention to.

Reviewed November 2026. Written from my own application in 2019 and from what has changed in the paperwork since.

The documents

- 10th and 12th marksheets and certificates

- Passport, valid for well beyond your course

- Birth certificate

- Police clearance certificate

- Medical fitness certificate

- Passport-size photographs, white background

- NEET scorecard, if you have one

The timeline

Allow three to four months from the first email to arrival. The acceptance letter is usually fast. The visa and the document gathering are the slow parts, and both get slower in the weeks before an intake. Once the visa file is complete, the office takes 20 to 25 days.

Start in February for a mid-year intake. Starting in May is how students end up paying express fees for a passport.

Before the MD, two requirements

The Philippine Doctor of Medicine is a postgraduate course. Enrolment needs a bachelor's degree and a pass in the National Medical Admission Test (NMAT). A student straight out of class 12 completes the pre-medical bachelor's degree first, which is the BSBio route, and that degree must itself be accredited by CHED.

Seven steps

## The sequence

1.

### Verify the college before you write to it

Two lists: the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in) and [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). This takes two minutes and saves five years. [My six](https://drdreams.in/colleges.md) are checked, but check them yourself anyway.

2.

### Email the international admissions office

Use the address on the college's own website, not a number forwarded on WhatsApp. Ask three things: the current fee sheet for the intake, the document list, and whether they have a BSBio route. [If you need that route](https://drdreams.in/without-neet.md), ask for the transfer conditions in writing.

3.

### Send the documents and get the acceptance letter

The letter names you and the course. This is the document the embassy, the airline and the immigration officer will all want to see. Keep the original, carry a folder of copies.

4.

### Apply for the student visa

The college issues a support letter. You apply at the Philippine embassy or consulate in India with that letter, your acceptance letter, your passport, photographs and the financial documents in the [visa checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md). Once the file is complete, the visa office takes 20 to 25 days. Keep every receipt. This is the one stage where a good consultant earns the fee, because a rejection costs a semester.

5.

### Book the flight, reserve the first month of housing

Book direct with the airline. Reserve a hostel through the student affairs office before you land. Look at apartments after you arrive and know the city, the commute and the neighbourhood.

6.

### Arrive, enrol, and register with immigration

Most colleges arrange airport pickup for international students. Enrolment is straightforward if your documents are complete. Then there is the local registration and, each year, a renewal. Put the renewal date in your phone the day you get it.

7.

### Survive the first month

SIM card, bank account, grocery run, and finding out which canteen is edible. This is the month where most students want to go home. [The life page](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md) covers it in detail.

Who does what

## Three parties, four decisions

Most of this process is email and patience. Three parties are involved and each has a fixed job. The four decisions in the middle are yours, and they are the ones that change the outcome.

### The four decisions

- Which college, and whether it is on the NMC list at the time you enrol

- Whether the total cost fits, hostel and visa renewals included

- Whether you can live in that city for five and a half years

- When FMGE preparation starts. Year two is the honest answer

### Where outside help is reasonable

- **The college** issues the acceptance letter, the visa support letter and the enrolment papers

- **The embassy** issues the 9(F) student visa once your file is complete

- **You** gather the documents, hold the passport and sit the interview

The stages run in a fixed order: enquiry, documents, acceptance letter, visa support letter, visa appointment, flight. Each stage has one thing that can stall it, and almost always it is a document rather than a decision. Knowing what comes next is most of the work.

The timeline that works backwards from an August start is on [the questions page](https://drdreams.in/faq.html#timing), and the documents themselves are on the [checklist page](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md).

If you do it yourself

## The four things that go wrong

- **A passport that expires mid-course.** Check the validity before you apply. Renewing a passport from abroad is a slow, expensive annoyance.

- **Documents that are not apostilled or authenticated.** Ask the college exactly which certificates need authentication and which do not. Guessing wastes a month.

- **Arriving before the hostel is ready.** Confirm the move-in date in writing. Hotels in Cebu and Manila are not cheap when you are paying by the night.

- **Missing a visa renewal.** Fines and a trip to immigration, and in a bad case a problem with your status. Set the reminder when you get the document, not when you remember.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) is the other half of this page.

Questions

## Before you start the paperwork

How long does the admission process take?

Allow three to four months from first email to arrival. The acceptance letter usually comes in two to four weeks. Document authentication and the visa appointment are what take the time, and both slow down in the weeks before an intake.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) covers the slowest part.

How long does the whole process take?

Allow three to four months from first email to arrival. The acceptance letter is usually quick. The visa and the document gathering are what take time, and both slow down in the weeks before an intake.

Can I apply to a Philippine medical college directly?

Yes. Every college has an international admissions office with an email address on its own website, and it handles foreign applicants directly.

You send your documents, the college sends the acceptance letter and a visa support letter, and you take those to the Philippine embassy. Nothing in that chain needs a middleman, though a licensed visa consultant can be worth it if your file is messy.

## What goes wrong

Four failures account for most of the pain in this process, and none of them is about intelligence. They are listed above. The documents are on the next page.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md)
          [The first month](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md)

Checklist

# Documents you need for MBBS in the Philippines

Two lists, and students usually mix them up. One set goes to the college. A slightly different set goes to the embassy. Here is both, with the format each document needs and the four mistakes that hold an application up for a month.

Reviewed November 2026. Built from the admission requirements published by the six colleges and the visa office document list for the current intake.

Start with the passport

Everything else is replaceable. A passport with less than eighteen months of validity is not, because renewing it from the Philippines means weeks without your travel document. Check the expiry date before you do anything else on this page.

The admission file is the smaller one. Most of it is paperwork you already have in a drawer, plus one document you have to earn: the NEET scorecard. The visa file repeats about half of it and adds the financial papers. Neither list is long. Both are unforgiving about names, dates and stamps.

List one

## What the college asks for

Colleges ask for these at different points. Some want scans before they issue the acceptance letter, some want attested hard copies on arrival. Ask which, in writing, so you are not carrying a folder across an ocean for nothing.

| Document | What it has to show | Format note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Class 10 marksheet and certificate | Date of birth as printed on your passport | Scan plus two attested copies |
| Class 12 marksheet and certificate | Physics, Chemistry and Biology, with the aggregate your college requires | Scan plus two attested copies |
| NEET scorecard | Your roll number, score and the year of the exam | Current year, or within the validity NMC allows |
| Passport | Eighteen months or more of validity, two blank pages | First and last page, plus the visa page once issued |
| Birth certificate | Full name, parents' names, place of birth | Municipal or national registry copy, usually apostilled |
| Passport photographs | White background, plain clothes, no glasses glare | Eight to ten copies, plus the digital file |
| Medical certificate | Fit to study, with a chest x-ray and HIV test at some colleges | On the college's own form if they send one |
| Police clearance or character certificate | No pending criminal case | From your district police or the passport office |
| Proof of funds | Tuition plus living costs for the first year | Six months of bank statements, plus a sponsor affidavit if the account is not yours |
| Application form and personal statement | Why medicine, why the Philippines, why this college | Half a page is enough. Two paragraphs written by you beat a template. |
| Transfer or migration certificate | Only if you are leaving an Indian college mid-course | Original, plus a no-objection letter from the Indian college |

Admission documents for the 2027 intake

If you already hold a bachelor's degree, add the degree certificate and marksheets. If you studied outside India, add an equivalence statement from the Philippine school. Gap years need a short affidavit explaining them, and nobody will be scandalised by one.

Authentication

## The stamp that takes the longest

A photocopy is not a document as far as the embassy is concerned. Indian certificates normally need three steps, in this order: notarisation, state attestation, then an apostille from the Ministry of External Affairs. Some states let you skip straight to the passport office route.

Budget three to four weeks. Tatkal exists, and it costs money. Do this while you are still choosing a college, because it is the slowest thing in the whole file and it has nothing to do with the college's speed.

One warning from experience: do not send originals anywhere until you have a complete set of attested photocopies in your own bag. Losing a birth certificate in transit is a two-month detour through your home district.

### The order that works

1. Passport renewed, if it expires within two years

2. Name spelling identical on every document

3. Marksheets and birth certificate notarised

4. State attestation, then MEA apostille

5. Scans sent to the college, hard copies in hand luggage

6. Eight photocopies of everything, in a plastic folder

List two

## What the visa office asks for

The student visa is a 9(F). The college issues a notice of acceptance and a support letter, and you take them to the Philippine embassy or consulate that covers your state. This is the document list the visa office hands out for the current intake. Confirm it with the college or the consulate before you submit, because the format rules are strict and the list changes.

1.

### Passport

The original, plus two colour copies.

2.

### PCC status tracker

A print of the tracker from the Passport Seva Portal.

3.

### Police Clearance Certificate

Through the Passport Seva Portal only. A PCC from a local police station is not accepted. Apply inside the stated window, and keep the original for submission.

4.

### NEET scorecard

Two colour copies.

5.

### NEET admit card

A black and white copy, as NTA issues it.

6.

### Bank statement, last six months

From the parent or sponsor's personal or salary account. A business account needs the GST registration certificate as well. Minimum closing balance Rs 3,00,000. Signed by the branch manager and sealed on every page, covering the full six months, with the balance showing at the time it was generated. An online statement without the signature and the seal is not accepted.

7.

### Affidavit of financial support and no objection

On Rs 100 bond paper, notarised. The same sponsor whose bank statement you submit signs it, and the notary is from the sponsor's district. The signature must match the PAN card, the later pages go on A4 green sheets, and the prescribed sample is followed.

8.

### Photographs

US visa size (2 x 2 inches, white background, about 80% face), five copies. Passport size, white background, five copies. US visa size with your name and the date on them, five copies.

9.

### Medical test report

From a NABH-accredited hospital only. Reports from pre-accreditation or NABL-accredited hospitals are not accepted. The report carries the medical officer's signature and the hospital seal, and your name must match the passport. Tests: chest X-ray (picture and report, A4), Hepatitis B (HBsAg), total blood examination, urine, stool, HIV and VDRL.

10.

### Aadhaar card

Colour copy. One for the student, one for the sponsor or parent whose bank statement and affidavit you submit.

11.

### Mark sheets

Class 10 and Class 12 originals, plus colour copies.

12.

### Vaccination certificate, if you have one

Download the International Travel Vaccination Certificate from CoWIN, with your passport number on it. If you were not vaccinated, ignore this one.

Four rules sit over the whole list. Every document must be genuine, complete and in the stated format. After you submit, the visa takes 20 to 25 days. A discrepancy, a fabricated document, a missing one or a badly prepared one delays the file. And the preparation is yours to do on time.

Some colleges have students enter on a temporary visitor visa and convert to the student visa after enrolment. Others insist on the 9(F) before you fly. Ask which route your intake uses, because the two need different paperwork and different timing.

After you land

## The documents that do not stop

The file does not close at immigration. In the first weeks the college helps you with the medical examination and the ACR I-Card, which is the identity card for foreign nationals. Keep eight photocopies of every page you have ever signed.

- **ACR I-Card.** Applied for through the college after enrolment. You will need it for almost everything else, including a bank account.

- **Annual report.** Foreign nationals file one every year within the first sixty days. Miss it and you pay a fine at the immigration office.

- **Visa renewal.** Put the date in your phone the day the stamp is issued, with a reminder a month earlier.

- **NBI clearance.** Needed later for hospital postings and for the internship year. It is a background check, not a college document.

Keep a digital copy

Scan everything to a cloud folder the day it is issued, and give a family member access. A lost file in Cebu is a week of emails. A lost file with no scans is a month of couriers.

Why files stall

## Four mistakes, in order of frequency

1.

### The name does not match

Initials expanded on one document and not another, a missing middle name, a spelling the clerk corrected by hand. Fix it at the source. An affidavit of one name is cheaper than a rejected visa file.

2.

### The passport expires mid-course

Five and a half years is a long time. Renew first, then apply, even if it costs you a month at the start.

3.

### The birth certificate is missing or unreadable

If it was never registered, get it registered now. A delayed registration is accepted; a blank space in the file is not.

4.

### The bank statement arrived yesterday

Funds that appear the week before the interview look borrowed, because they usually are. Six months of ordinary movement is more convincing than a large deposit the day before.

Questions

## About the paperwork

What bank balance does the student visa need?

The visa office asks for a six month statement from the parent or sponsor, with a closing balance of at least Rs 3,00,000. It has to be signed by the branch manager and sealed on every page. An online statement without those is rejected, and a business account also needs the GST registration certificate.

Deposits that appear the week before you apply read as borrowed. Six months of ordinary movement, ending above the minimum, is what the file is looking for.

Do my documents need an apostille for the Philippines?

Usually yes for the certificates the college forwards to the Philippine authorities, mainly the birth certificate and the class 12 marksheet. India and the Philippines are both part of the Apostille Convention, so a Ministry of External Affairs apostille is normally accepted.

Colleges differ on which documents they want authenticated and when, so ask the admissions office for the list in writing before you spend money on attestation.

How long does authentication take in India?

Plan for two to four weeks on the standard route: notary, then state Home Department or Regional Passport Office attestation, then the MEA apostille. Tatkal services in some states cut it to a week, at a price.

Start before the visa stage, not during it. This is the step that most often delays an intake.

Can I apply before my NEET result comes out?

Yes. Colleges issue conditional acceptance letters on the basis of your class 12 marks and your NEET roll number, and the scorecard is added when it arrives.

You cannot complete the visa file without it, because the embassy asks for the scorecard and NMC eligibility depends on the score.

What if my name is spelled differently on two documents?

Fix it before you apply. A mismatch between the passport, the marksheet and the birth certificate is the most common reason a file goes back, and it is much harder to correct from Cebu than from your own district office.

Get a corrected certificate or a one-name affidavit, then apply. [Tell me](https://drdreams.in/contact.md) if a college told you otherwise and I will look into it.
