Five and a half years

# Student life in the Philippines for Indian students

I spent five and a half years in Cebu, and the first one was the hard one. Not the anatomy. The food, the heat, the accent, the silence in a room where nobody knows your name yet. This is the page I wish someone had written for me before I flew.

Reviewed November 2026. First hand, from Cebu. Manila and Davao checked against students who studied in both.

Cebu at night. Small enough to learn in a month, big enough that you keep finding places.

## The first month is logistics, not medicine

I landed in June, walked out of the airport into air that felt like a wet towel, and spent my first night in a room with a fan that clicked all night. The next two weeks were not about medicine at all. They were a SIM card, a bank account, a medical check for the visa paperwork, a mattress, a bucket, and working out which canteen would not make me ill.

Nobody tells you this part, and it makes the first month feel like a mistake. It is not. It is the same fortnight every international student has, and it passes faster than it feels like it will. By the third week I had a routine, a place to eat, and two people I could text at eleven at night.

If you remember one thing from this page, make it this: the first month is not a test of whether you are cut out for medicine. It is a test of whether you can ask strangers for help. Ask the senior, ask the landlord, ask the security guard. Everyone I asked helped me.

## Food, which is the whole first month

Filipino food is not Indian food, and pretending otherwise is how students end up eating instant noodles for a semester. It is rice-based, often sweet, often pork, and rarely spicy the way you expect. I ate rice and egg for dinner more often in my first year than I will admit to anyone in person.

It is also genuinely good once you stop comparing it to home. Lechon, sinigang, a proper breakfast of garlic rice and dried fish. The trick was to stop looking for dal and start eating what the city eats, then keep Indian food for the days I needed it.

The practical hierarchy: a college mess with Indian cooks is the easiest first year. Manila has enough of an Indian population that spices and restaurants are easy to find. Cebu has Indian restaurants and a few spice shops, but not around every campus. Davao is thinner, and Sasa, where Jose Maria sits, is thinner still.

Where there is no mess, students cook. Before I left home my mother taught me dal, rice and one vegetable, badly, in an afternoon. It was enough. Carry turmeric, cumin, coriander powder, garam masala and chilli powder in checked luggage, because those are the expensive, hard-to-find part. A rice cooker and an induction plate did the rest for five years.

## Rent, by city

I stayed in a hostel for the first year and moved into an apartment with two friends after that. The hostel was plain: bunk bed, shared bathroom, fan, and a curfew I did not love. It was also close to campus, secure, and it meant I did not have to negotiate a lease in a country I had never lived in. For year one, that trade is worth it.

The apartment was cheaper per head and much better for morale. It also taught me that you cannot know who you can live with until you have lived with them, so keep the first lease short and do not sign with someone you met last month.

Manila is the expensive one. Cebu sits in the middle. Davao is the cheapest of the three. Ask students who are there now rather than the admissions office: the office quotes the hostel, and students know what rent actually is.

## Safety, without the hysteria

Five and a half years in Cebu and I never had a serious problem. That is one person's experience, not a guarantee, so here is what people actually mean when they say be careful. All of it is ordinary city sense, and most of it is the same advice your parents gave you about Delhi or Mumbai.

- Do not walk alone at night in an area you do not know yet.

- Do not carry large amounts of cash or wear obvious gold.

- Use Grab rather than unmarked taxis, especially at night and especially in Manila.

- Keep your passport, visa documents and a set of photocopies in different places.

- Learn the local emergency numbers and the college security number in your first week.

Cebu and Davao are calmer than the reputation of Manila suggests. The real risk to your future is not crime. It is drifting for two years and then panicking about FMGE, which has ended more Indian students in the Philippines than anything in the news.

## The accent, and the language

Classes are in English. I understood maybe two thirds of my first lecture and most of the rest by the end of the month. Filipino English runs closer to American English in rhythm than Indian English does, and lecturers switch to Tagalog or Cebuano among themselves, which is not rude, just normal.

Learn a few phrases. "Salamat" for thank you, "magkano" for how much, and a greeting or two. My Cebuano never got past that, and it still changed how people treated me more than any amount of grammar would have.

## Weather, and what it does to your wardrobe

Hot and humid most of the year, with hard rain from roughly June to November. Light cotton clothes, a good umbrella, and shoes that survive a flooded street. I went through three cheap umbrellas before I bought one that cost more and lasted four years.

Air conditioning is standard in classrooms and most hostels, sometimes as a paid extra. A room with air conditioning and a room without are two different rents, and the difference shows up in June.

## Money, month to month

Beyond tuition and rent, my month was food, transport, phone data, and whatever the weekend cost. Cooking cut that down more than anything else I did. Manila costs more than Cebu for the same life, and Davao less.

Open a local bank account in the first month. Carrying cash for a semester is both risky and expensive, and paying tuition through a bank leaves a receipt, which matters if anything is ever disputed. Ask the college which bank they work with for international students, and bring the documents that bank will ask for.

## Homesickness, honestly

The first semester is the hardest and the brochures do not mention it. I missed food, my family, and being understood without effort. Around month three I was fairly sure I had made a mistake. Almost everyone I know went through the same week.

What helped, in order: a routine, three or four people I ate with, one call home at a fixed time each week, and something physical that was not studying. What did not help was going home in the first semester, because I came back and started the whole adjustment again.

By second year Cebu was a place I lived in rather than a place I was stuck in. That happens to most people, and it happens later than you want it to.

## What I would pack again

- Light cotton clothes, a few formal outfits for clinical postings, and a white coat if the college does not issue one.

- Basic spices, sealed properly, in checked luggage.

- Any prescription medicine you take, with the prescription, in its original packaging.

- A universal adapter and a power bank.

- Photocopies of every document, and digital copies in cloud storage.

- One thing that makes the room feel like yours. It matters more than it sounds, and I still have mine.

Questions

## The three every parent asks

Is the Philippines safe for Indian students?

Cebu, Davao and most student areas of Metro Manila are safe if you use ordinary city sense: do not walk alone in unfamiliar areas at night, do not flash money, and stay in groups when you are new. I lived in Cebu for five and a half years without a serious incident, which is one person's experience and not a guarantee.

Will I get Indian food?

In Manila, yes, easily. In Cebu and Davao it depends on the college and the neighbourhood. Where there is no mess, students cook. Learn three dishes before you leave and carry basic spices in your checked luggage. I cooked for five years and it was fine, and cheaper than the alternative.

What should I pack?

Light cotton clothes, formal clothes for clinical postings, a white coat if your college does not issue one, basic spices, medicines you trust, and a power adapter. Do not fill a suitcase with winter clothes or gadgets you will not use.

## The money and the paperwork

Life is the part students worry about and the part that usually works out. Cost is the part that surprises families.

For current students

# Study resources for medical students in the Philippines

A study framework for the five and a half years, plus the notes, question banks and practical guides that will be added here as they are ready.

Last reviewed November 2026.

This section is being built

Subject notes, question banks and practical guides will be added here as they are prepared. Nothing is downloadable yet, and no file on this page is a promise of what is coming. The study framework below is ready to use now.

## On this page

1. The subject map, year by year

2. How the Philippine curriculum is taught

3. A weekly study system

4. Using Indian resources alongside

5. FMGE from first year

6. Learning on the ward

7. Notes and downloads

## The subject map, year by year

Philippine medical schools follow the American shape: pre-clinical sciences, then para-clinical sciences, then clinical rotations, then internship. The names and the order vary a little between colleges, so treat this as the common pattern and confirm the exact sequence with your own curriculum.

| Stage | Subjects | What it feels like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First year | Anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, histology, embryology, medical ethics | Volume. You are memorising a new language and a new body at the same time. |
| Second year | Pathology, pharmacology, microbiology, parasitology, forensic medicine, community medicine, physical diagnosis | The mechanisms click, and the clinical vocabulary starts to make sense. |
| Third year | Medicine, surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, radiology, psychiatry, dermatology | Wards, clerkships, patient histories, and the first time you present a case. |
| Fourth year | Clinical rotations, specialities, review, internship preparation | You are in the hospital most days. The exam is closer than it feels. |
| Internship | Rotating departments under supervision | Long shifts, real responsibility, and the transition from student to doctor. |

The usual subject sequence in a Philippine MD programme.

Your college may call the years Level 1 to Level 4, or use a different split. The fee sheets from Gullas, DMSF, Jose Maria and Brokenshire use "Level 1" and semesters. That is an administrative label, not a different course.

## How the Philippine curriculum is taught

Most colleges use lectures, laboratory sessions and small-group discussions in the pre-clinical years, then ward-based teaching in the clinical years. The lecture is the skeleton. The learning happens in the laboratory, the group work and the past papers.

Two local habits are worth adopting. The first is the "trans" or transcription: students rewrite or summarise lecture material into a shared document. It is efficient, and it is also how a batch builds a common set of notes. The second is recitation: faculty ask questions in class, and you are expected to answer. If you are shy, practice answering aloud before you go.

Attendance rules are stricter than many Indian students expect. A missed laboratory or ward session can cost you the subject, not just the notes. Read the college's attendance policy in the first week, not the week before the exam.

## A weekly study system

The students who do well do not study more hours than everyone else. They study with a rhythm. A simple system that survives a five and a half year course:

1. **Preview before the lecture.** Ten minutes with the headings is enough. You will recognise the words instead of hearing them for the first time.

2. **Rewrite the lecture the same day.** A one-page summary in your own words, not a copy of the slide.

3. **Do questions twice a week.** Start with the topics you covered that week, not the whole syllabus.

4. **Keep one review day.** Sunday morning for the week's summaries, and nothing new.

5. **Teach one topic to a friend.** If you cannot explain it without the notes, you do not know it yet.

| Day | Focus | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monday to Friday | Preview, lecture, same-day summary | 2 to 3 hours outside class |
| Tuesday and Thursday | Questions on the week's topics | 45 minutes each |
| Saturday | Practical or ward notes, weak topic | 2 hours |
| Sunday | Weekly review, one past paper | 2 to 3 hours |

A repeatable week, not a timetable you abandon in week two.

Adjust the hours to your college. The point is the repetition, not the number.

## Using Indian resources alongside

Indian textbooks are cheaper, more exam-oriented and closer to the FMGE syllabus. Philippine textbooks are closer to your lectures and your local exams. Use both, but do not try to read both cover to cover.

A practical split: use the Philippine material to pass the college exam, and one Indian review book per subject to keep the FMGE vocabulary alive. For anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pathology, pharmacology and microbiology, an Indian review book plus your lecture notes is usually enough for the college exam. For community medicine and forensic medicine, the Indian syllabus differs more, so follow your college first and bridge later.

Do not buy a new set of books every year. A good review book, a question bank and your own notes beat a shelf of unopened titles.

## FMGE from first year

The FMGE clock starts in first year, whether you like it or not. The exam tests the Indian undergraduate syllabus, and the subjects you learn in first year are the ones you will have forgotten by the time you graduate.

You do not need to study for FMGE every day in first year. You need to keep the Indian thread alive: one review book per subject, a question bank you add to slowly, and a note of the topics your Philippine course does not cover. By the clinical years, that thread is the difference between a six month revision and a two year panic.

The [FMGE and NExT page](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next.md) has the full year-by-year plan.

## Learning on the ward

Clinical years reward a different skill from pre-clinical years. You are not memorising a list. You are learning to ask a question, examine a patient, and present a plan. Three habits that help:

- **Carry a small notebook.** Write the case in your own words after you see it. The act of writing is the learning.

- **Present every case you can.** Even to a fellow student. The first ten presentations are terrible. The eleventh is better.

- **Ask one question per ward round.** Not to show off. To make yourself follow the reasoning.

Foreign students are allowed hands-on work in Philippine hospitals, which is one of the reasons to choose the country. Use that access. Watching is not the same as doing, and the difference shows up in the exam and in your first Indian internship.

## Notes and downloads

This page will hold subject-wise notes, question banks, practical and OSCE guides, and study planners. They will be added as they are ready, and each file will say which subject and year it covers. Nothing is uploaded yet, so there is no download link to click and no email form to fill.

If you have notes from your own college that you are willing to share, the [contact page](https://drdreams.in/contact.md) explains how to send them. They will be checked before they are published, and you will be credited if you want to be.

Questions

## Study questions students ask

Are Philippine medical books different from Indian books?

The content is the same medicine, but the emphasis and the exam style differ. Use Philippine material for your college exams and one Indian review book per subject to keep the FMGE syllabus familiar.

When should I start FMGE preparation?

First year, slowly. One review book per subject and a question bank you add to over time. The students who start in the final year are the ones who run out of time.

Are the notes on this page free?

The study material will be free when it is added. Nothing is downloadable yet, and there is no paid course behind this page.

What is a "trans" in a Philippine medical school?

A transcription, usually a student-made summary of a lecture shared with the batch. It is useful, but it is not a substitute for the lecture or the textbook.

How many hours a day should I study?

Two to three focused hours outside class is a realistic baseline. More matters less than consistency and active recall. A weekly review day is worth more than a late-night cram.

Six colleges

# Medical colleges in the Philippines for Indian students

Six, not sixty. One of these was my own college, I visited three more, and I know graduates from all six. Every page carries the cons we would tell a cousin, because a page without cons is an advertisement.

Reviewed November 2026. The ratings are subjective judgements, not an official ranking. Verify every fact that matters to your money.

| College | City | My rating | Best for | FMGE coaching on campus | Indian batch | Indian food |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**GCM Gullas**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md) | Cebu City | ★★★★★ | Lowest entry cost with coaching included | Yes | Large | Limited |
| [**Southwestern**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/southwestern.md) | Cebu City | ★★★★☆ | Hospital rotations, small Indian crowd | No | Small | Okay |
| [**Perpetual Help**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/perpetual.md) | Las Piñas, Metro Manila | ★★★★☆ | The Indian community and food | Yes | Largest | Good |
| [**DMSF**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/dmsf.md) | Davao City | ★★★★☆ | Clinical volume and the anatomy lab | Yes | Medium | Good |
| [**Brokenshire**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/brokenshire.md) | Davao City | ★★★☆☆ | Small batches and faculty attention | Yes | Small | Good |
| [**Jose Maria**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/jmc.md) | Sasa, Davao City | ★★★☆☆ | The tightest budget | Yes | Very small | Very limited |

Side by side. Scroll sideways on a phone.

Fees: published 2026-2027 sheets exist for Gullas, DMSF, Jose Maria and Brokenshire, and they are on the [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md) and on each college page. Southwestern and Perpetual publish theirs on request. College fee sheets change every intake, so confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay.

2027 intake

## Which colleges are taking admissions now

Philippine medical colleges run one main intake a year. Classes for the 2027 intake begin in August and September, and applications stay open until the batch fills. The dates below are what each admissions office told me in November 2026; confirm the current position before you pay anything.

| College | City | Applications | Classes begin | Admissions contact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**GCM Gullas**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md) | Cebu City | Open | August 2027 | International office, on the college site |
| [**Southwestern**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/southwestern.md) | Cebu City | Open | August 2027 | International office, on the college site |

| [**Jose Maria**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/jmc.md) | Sasa, Davao City | Open | August 2027 | International office, on the college site |

Application status, November 2026

All six accept foreign students directly through their own admissions offices. The bottleneck in every case is the same three things: the NEET scorecard, the document authentication, and the embassy appointment. Start in the spring and there is time for all three.

Do this yourself

## How to check any college in two minutes

Before you trust this page or anyone else's, check the two lists that decide whether the degree is worth anything in India.

1.

### Open the NMC list

[nmc.org.in](https://www.nmc.org.in), then the list of recognised foreign medical institutions. Search the college name. If it is absent, stop.

2.

### Open the world directory

[search.wdoms.org](https://search.wdoms.org). NMC's 2026 notice relies on this directory for verification, so a college missing here is a risk even if a brochure says otherwise.

3.

### Then read the college's own fee sheet

Not a forwarded PDF. The version from the admissions office, with the year printed on it.

About the ratings

Five stars does not mean Harvard. It means that for an Indian student with a normal budget, we would have few reservations about sending a younger cousin there.

Three stars means the college is legitimate and NMC-listed, but there is a specific trade we would want you to accept with your eyes open: a small hospital, a smaller batch, or a city with very little Indian food.

No college gets five stars here for facilities. The best facility in the Philippines is still not a match for a good Indian government college. What you are buying here is a seat, English-medium teaching and clinical access.

## Before you shortlist

Rank any shortlist on three things: NMC listing, total cost, and whether the hospital is big enough to put you in front of patients. Each college page says which of those is the weakest.

[Compare the real costs](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md)
          [Check the NMC rules](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules.md)

source: https://drdreams.in/glossary.html
updated: 2026-11-22

Reference

# Glossary of terms

The words that appear in college emails, NMC notices and conversations with seniors, defined in one or two sentences each.

Last reviewed November 2026.

How to use this page

If a college email, an NMC notice or a senior uses a term you do not know, find it here. The links go to the page that explains the thing, not just the word.

Terms are grouped by their first letter. Each entry is one or two sentences, because the point is to let you read the next page without stopping.

## A

APMC

Association of Philippine Medical Colleges. The association of medical schools in the Philippines, not an Indian regulator.

Apostille

A stamp that authenticates a public document for use in another country. India is part of the Hague Apostille Convention, so many Indian documents are apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs rather than legalised by an embassy.

## B

BSBio

Bachelor of Science in Biology, the pre-medical year some Philippine universities offer. It is not a medical degree and it does not replace NEET.

## C

CHED

Commission on Higher Education, the Philippine government body that oversees higher education, including medical schools.

Clerkship

The clinical years of the MD, when students rotate through hospital departments and clerk patients under supervision.

CRMI

Compulsory Rotating Medical Internship. The twelve month internship in India that foreign graduates complete after passing FMGE or NExT.

## E

ECFMG

Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates. The body that certifies international medical graduates for US residency applications.

## F

FMGE

Foreign Medical Graduate Examination. The screening exam Indian foreign graduates sit before registration. Conducted by NBEMS.

FMGL 2021

The Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations, 2021. The NMC rules that apply to students who enrolled on or after 18 November 2021.

## I

Internship

The supervised final year of the MD in the Philippines, done in a hospital. Separate from the Indian CRMI.

## L

Level

The administrative name some Philippine colleges use for a year of the MD, as in Level 1 or Level 2. It is not a different qualification.

## M

MD

Doctor of Medicine. In the Philippines, the primary medical degree, roughly equivalent to MBBS for Indian registration when the college is NMC-listed.

MEA

Ministry of External Affairs, India. It authenticates or apostilles documents for use abroad.

## N

NBEMS

National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences. The body that conducts FMGE, NEET-PG and other postgraduate medical exams in India.

NEET

National Eligibility cum Entrance Test. The Indian entrance exam for medical courses. NMC requires it for Indian students who intend to practise in India.

NEET-PG

The Indian entrance exam for MD, MS and diploma postgraduate seats.

NExT

National Exit Test. The exam being introduced to replace FMGE and unify the final-year and licensing examinations. Check the current status for your batch.

NMC

National Medical Commission. India's medical regulator since 2020, replacing the Medical Council of India.

## O

OSCE

Objective Structured Clinical Examination. A practical exam with stations that test history taking, examination and communication.

## P

PGI

Postgraduate Institute. A term used loosely for postgraduate medical institutes. Not a qualification by itself.

PRC

Professional Regulation Commission, the Philippine body that licenses professionals, including physicians.

## R

Recitation

The classroom habit of being called on to answer questions aloud. Common in Philippine medical schools.

RLE

Related Learning Experience. The supervised clinical practice hours built into Philippine health courses. The term is more common in nursing than in medicine.

Rotation

A block of clinical training in one department, such as medicine, surgery or paediatrics.

## S

Semester

Half of an academic year. Philippine colleges often quote fees per semester rather than per year.

## T

Trans

A student-made transcription or summary of a lecture, shared within a batch.

## U

USMLE

United States Medical Licensing Examination. The exam series for US medical licensure, usually taken alongside ECFMG certification.

## W

WDOMS

World Directory of Medical Schools. A directory of medical schools run by WFME and FAIMER. NMC uses it for verification.

## 9

9F visa

The Philippine student visa category. Many students enter on a temporary visa and convert to 9F after enrolment, so confirm the current process with the college and embassy.

# Colleges

Cebu City

# GCM Gullas College of Medicine

The lowest entry cost of the six, with FMGE coaching inside the campus. It is also the biggest batch and the plainest hostel. If your budget is the deciding factor, this is where to start.

Reviewed November 2026. Written from Cebu, with information from Gullas graduates and students.

## The facts

City

Cebu City, Cebu

Programme

Doctor of Medicine

Duration

About 5.5 years with internship

Language

English

FMGE coaching

Yes, on campus

Official site

[gullascollegeofmedicine.com](https://gullascollegeofmedicine.com)

The short version

Best value for money among the six. Cebu is safe, the hospital exposure is decent, and the campus has FMGE coaching that you do not have to arrange separately.

Go in expecting a large Indian batch, a hostel that is functional rather than comfortable, and a campus that feels busy rather than calm.

Where this comes from

Time was spent on this campus during five and a half years in Cebu, and the page draws on graduates and current students. I did not study medicine at Gullas, so the classroom detail comes from them.

The good

## What works here

- **The entry cost is the lowest of the six.** For a family that has a hard ceiling, this is the college that keeps the whole five years inside it.

- **FMGE coaching is on campus.** That sounds small until year four, when the alternative is an online course, a lot of self-discipline and nobody checking whether you watched it.

- **Cebu is the easier city.** Smaller than Manila, cheaper, and calmer. Students move around at night here in a way they do not in parts of Metro Manila.

- **Hospital exposure is real.** The affiliated hospitals are busy, and students get into the wards rather than watching from a corridor.

- **Food is manageable.** Limited compared with Manila, but Cebu has Indian restaurants and spice shops, and the college area has places that will cook for you.

- **Large Indian batch.** If you are the kind of student who needs company to survive the first year, this is a feature, not a flaw.

The trade

## What you give up

- **The batch is large.** You will not be a name to most faculty in the first two years. If you learn by being noticed and questioned, that is a real cost.

- **The hostel is basic.** Clean enough, not comfortable. Do not arrive expecting air conditioning and privacy at the lowest price quoted.

- **Competition for attention.** A big batch means fewer minutes per student in practicals. The students who do well here are the ones who ask first.

- **It is a value pick, not a prestige pick.** Nobody in India will be impressed by the name. What matters is the NMC listing and your FMGE score.

Fit

## Who should pick it

A student with a clear budget ceiling who does not need to be the only Indian in the room, and who will use the on-campus coaching instead of treating it as optional. It also suits families who want the city to be the safe, boring part of the decision.

Not for

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs small classes and personal attention, anyone who cannot handle a crowd, and anyone whose plan depends on a comfortable hostel. Look at [Brokenshire](https://drdreams.in/colleges/brokenshire.md) for attention or [Perpetual](https://drdreams.in/colleges/perpetual.md) for a bigger Indian community.

Money

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

| Particular | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Enrolment and admission fee | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Book fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | 1,25,000 PHP (Rs 1,80,966) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 14,000 PHP (Rs 20,268) |

Fee sheet, GCM Gullas College of Medicine, 2026-2027

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, on the Gullas and KINGS campus.

- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.

- Refund: the enrolment fee is not refunded.

**Campus facilities:** 3D Anatomage, laboratory, classroom, auditorium, hospital, library.

**What the admissions package includes:** MEA and foreign-affairs authentication, apostille of academic documents, visa appointment and preparation, embassy visa interview fee, visa from the Philippines embassy in India, foreign-exchange assistance, one India-Philippines flight ticket, airport pickup and transfer to the hostel, and a Philippines mobile SIM.

Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.

Money

## What to ask the college for

The sheet above is the 2026-2027 figure published by the college. Fees change every intake, so confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay. Ask the admissions office for these things as well:

1.

### The current fee sheet, with the year printed on it

Tuition per year, not per semester, and the total for the full programme.

2.

### What the hostel costs, separately

Per month or per semester, and what is included. Ask whether air conditioning is extra.

3.

### Which fees are refundable

If your visa is refused, what comes back and what does not.

4.

### Whether FMGE coaching is included

On campus, and whether it is part of tuition or a separate charge later.

5.

### The internship arrangement

Which hospital, for how long, and whether it satisfies NMC's onsite requirement.

6.

### The written confirmation of your seat

On college letterhead, before you transfer money to anyone.

Then compare the totals on the [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md), including flights and visa renewals. The cheapest first year is not always the cheapest degree.

## Before you pay anyone

Verify, in this order

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet, from the college's own admissions office, not from the person asking you to pay.

If a broker cannot tell you where the college appears on those two lists, that is your answer.

Official website: [gullascollegeofmedicine.com](https://gullascollegeofmedicine.com). The international admissions contact is on that site, and it is the address you should write to.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) is worth ten minutes before any payment.

Cebu City

# Southwestern University

Where I studied. The hospital rotations are the reason to come, and the smaller Indian batch is the reason it is possible to concentrate. Nobody will hand you FMGE coaching here, so plan for that yourself.

Reviewed November 2026. Written from five and a half years here, graduating in 2025.

## The facts

City

Cebu City, Cebu

Programme

Doctor of Medicine

Duration

About 5.5 years with internship

Language

English

FMGE coaching

No, arrange your own

Official site

[swu.edu.ph](https://swu.edu.ph)

The short version

A solid, established university with genuinely busy hospitals. Small Indian batch, so less distraction and less support at the same time.

The admin is slow. Learn to follow up in person, keep photocopies of everything, and start FMGE preparation with an outside course from first year.

Where this comes from

Five and a half years here, graduating in 2025. Everything on this page is first hand, which also means it is biased in the college's favour. Read the cons twice.

The good

## What works here

- **The clinical years are the real thing.** Busy wards, real patients, and students are expected to work rather than observe. Students deliver babies and assist in theatre here.

- **Faculty who have practised.** The clinicians teaching you have seen the cases they describe. That sounds obvious. It is not universal.

- **Small Indian batch.** Fewer countrymen means more English spoken, more Filipino friends, and less time in a comfort bubble. That is the difference between passing and coasting.

- **An established university.** The campus has been running long enough that the processes, however slow, exist and work. You are not the first Indian student anyone has seen.

- **Cebu itself.** Cheaper than Manila, safer than the reputation of big cities, and small enough that you learn it in a month.

The trade

## What you give up

- **No in-house FMGE coaching.** This is the big one. At Gullas or Perpetual the coaching comes to you. Here you buy an online course and hope you have the discipline. Many students do not.

- **Administration is slow.** Documents, transcripts and letters take longer than they should. Budget extra weeks for anything official, and never leave it to the last week before a deadline.

- **The campus can feel impersonal.** It is a large university, not a small college. You are one of many, especially in the first two years.

- **Indian food is only okay.** You will find it, but a decent Indian mess is not around the corner. Learn to cook.

- **Quiet social life if you do not make an effort.** Cebu is fun, but nothing is arranged for you. The first six months are lonely unless you join something.

Fit

## Who should pick it

A self-directed student who wants the hospital more than the classroom, who will buy an FMGE course without being told, and who does not need a large Indian crowd to feel at home. It also suits someone who wants a university name that carries some weight locally in Cebu.

Not for

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs structured coaching built into the campus, anyone who struggles without a peer group from home, and anyone who gets defeated by paperwork. [Gullas](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md) solves the first, [Perpetual](https://drdreams.in/colleges/perpetual.md) the second.

Money

## What to ask the college for

**Fees and facilities:** this college does not publish a fee sheet or a facilities list online. Ask the admissions office for the current fee sheet, the affiliated teaching hospital, and the on-campus facilities list, in writing.

Fees change by intake, so no number is printed here. Write to the admissions office and ask for these in writing:

1.

### The current annual fee sheet

With the academic year printed on it, and the total across the whole programme.

2.

### Hostel cost and what it includes

Monthly or per semester, and how far it is from the hospital you will rotate in.

3.

### The refund policy in writing

Especially if the visa is refused or you withdraw before enrolment.

4.

### The internship hospital and duration

Which hospital, how long, and confirmation that it meets NMC's onsite requirement.

5.

### Which fees are payable in pesos on arrival

Some charges are local and do not appear in the quotation you get in India.

Then add flights, visa renewal, insurance and living costs. The [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md) walks through every line.

## Before you pay anyone

Verify, in this order

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the college itself.

A Southwestern seat quoted at a price that does not match the college sheet is carrying something extra, and that something is not a college fee.

Official website: [swu.edu.ph](https://swu.edu.ph). Use the contact on that site, not a number forwarded on WhatsApp.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) for this intake.

Las Piñas, Metro Manila

# University of Perpetual Help

The softest landing of the six. The largest Indian community, real Indian food, and FMGE coaching built into campus life. You pay for that in Manila traffic and a higher monthly budget.

Reviewed November 2026. Based on close friends who studied here and several campus visits.

## The facts

City

Las Piñas, Metro Manila

Programme

Doctor of Medicine

Duration

About 5.5 years with internship

Language

English

FMGE coaching

Yes, on campus

Official site

[perpetualdalta.edu.ph](https://perpetualdalta.edu.ph)

The short version

The choice to make if you know you will struggle with loneliness or with cooking. You will find a seniors' network, an Indian mess, and people who have done the FMGE before you.

What you will not find is quiet. Metro Manila is loud, slow to cross, and more expensive than Cebu or Davao.

Where this comes from

Close friends studied medicine here and the campus has been visited more than once. This page is their experience plus observation, not a degree from Perpetual. Where something is uncertain, it says so.

The good

## What works here

- **The Indian community is the biggest of the six.** Seniors who have cleared FMGE, notes passed down, someone to tell you which hostel is a trap on your first week. That network is worth more than it sounds.

- **FMGE coaching is established.** Not a token weekend session. The coaching here has a track record and it runs alongside the course.

- **Indian food is genuinely available.** Restaurants, grocery stores with spices, and mess options. If food is the thing that would break you, this is the college that removes it.

- **Hospital exposure is solid.** Metro Manila hospitals see a very wide case mix, and students get into the wards.

- **Easy to reach India.** More flights out of Manila than out of Cebu or Davao, which matters when there is an emergency at home.

The trade

## What you give up

- **Traffic and pollution.** A commute that should take twenty minutes takes an hour. That hour comes out of your study time, every day, for five years.

- **A higher cost of living.** Rent, food and transport all cost more than Cebu or Davao. Budget accordingly, not by the college's first-year quote.

- **Distraction.** A large Indian batch can be a comfort or a party, depending on the company you keep. Several students say they studied better after moving apartments away from the group.

- **You are one of many.** Large cohort, and the campus is a business. Do not expect to be chased if you fall behind.

Fit

## Who should pick it

A student who knows their limit and wants support built in: people from home, food from home, and coaching in the building. It also suits a family that values being able to reach the student with a short flight.

Not for

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs quiet and cheap, and anyone who is easily pulled into a crowd. If you know you will spend more evenings out than in the library, a smaller batch in Cebu or Davao is a better fit. See [Southwestern](https://drdreams.in/colleges/southwestern.md) or [Brokenshire](https://drdreams.in/colleges/brokenshire.md).

Money

## What to ask the college for

**Fees and facilities:** this college does not publish a fee sheet or a facilities list online. Ask the admissions office for the current fee sheet, the affiliated teaching hospital, and the on-campus facilities list, in writing.

Manila changes the monthly arithmetic more than the college does. Ask for both:

1.

### The current fee sheet, with the year on it

Annual tuition and the total across the programme, not a per-semester figure that hides the rest.

2.

### Hostel cost, and what a nearby apartment costs

Ask students, not the office. The office will quote the hostel; the students will tell you what rent actually is.

3.

### Whether coaching is included or separate

And what it costs in the years it runs.

4.

### The refund policy if the visa is refused

In writing, before any transfer.

5.

### Which hospital you rotate in

And how you get there. In Manila, distance is measured in time, not kilometres.

Compare the full five-year total, not the first year. The [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md) shows how the city changes the number.

## Before you pay anyone

Verify, in this order

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

Perpetual is one of the most recommended colleges in the country, because it is popular and easy to reach. Popular is not the same as right for you.

Official website: [perpetualdalta.edu.ph](https://perpetualdalta.edu.ph).

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) for this intake.

Davao City

# Davao Medical School Foundation

The clinical experience people talk about is real. High patient flow, a useful anatomy lab, and FMGE coaching run by Indian doctors. You pay more for it than you would in Cebu.

Reviewed November 2026. Based on senior friends who studied here and a campus visit.

## The facts

City

Davao City, Davao del Sur

Programme

Doctor of Medicine

Duration

About 5.5 years with internship

Language

English

FMGE coaching

Yes, by Indian doctors

Official site

[dmsf.edu.ph](https://dmsf.edu.ph)

The short version

The pick if you care most about seeing cases and less about the city. The anatomy lab is genuinely better than the one at Southwestern, and the hospitals are busy.

The trade is money and distance. Davao is further from India, and the fee is higher than the Cebu colleges.

Where this comes from

Not a DMSF graduate. The information comes from senior friends who graduated from DMSF and from a campus visit. The classroom detail is theirs; the comparison with Cebu is first hand.

The good

## What works here

- **The anatomy lab is a real advantage.** The 3D table helps when a cadaver is not available. It is a teaching aid, not a substitute for dissection, but it makes first year easier to understand.

- **High patient inflow.** You see a wider variety of cases here than in smaller hospitals, and variety is what makes clinical years useful.

- **FMGE coaching by Indian doctors.** People who sat the exam themselves, teaching for it. Different from a generic campus course.

- **A functioning Indian mess.** Food is settled, which removes a first-year stressor that most students underestimate.

- **Davao is calmer and safer than its reputation.** Five and a half years in Cebu and several trips to Davao, with no trouble walking at night. It is a smaller, more orderly city than Manila.

The trade

## What you give up

- **The fee is higher than the Cebu colleges.** You are paying for the lab, the hospitals and the coaching. Decide whether those are worth the difference to you.

- **Distance.** A longer trip home, fewer direct flights, and an extra connection when there is an emergency. For some families that is the deciding factor.

- **It can feel isolating.** Smaller city, smaller Indian crowd than Manila, and less to do on a weekend. If you need a social scene, Davao will not provide it.

- **Being the best-funded student does not make it the best fit.** A few students arrive expecting the fee to solve motivation. It does not.

Fit

## Who should pick it

A student whose priority is clinical exposure, whose family can absorb the higher fee, and who is comfortable in a quieter city. It suits someone who wants coaching from people who have cleared the exam rather than a general prep course.

Not for

## Who should skip it

Anyone on a tight budget, anyone who needs a big Indian crowd, and anyone who will be flying home more than once a year. The cheaper Cebu options do the job. See [Gullas](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md) or [Southwestern](https://drdreams.in/colleges/southwestern.md).

Money

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

| Particular | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Enrolment fee | Rs 2,50,000 |
| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,50,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,50,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Book fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | USD 2,750 (Rs 2,54,871) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) |

Fee sheet, Davao Medical School Foundation, 2026-2027

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, on the DMSF and KINGS campus.

- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.

- Refund: the enrolment fee is not refunded.

- Internship: the fee for the one-year internship is discussed at the time of internship.

**Campus facilities:** Hospital, hostel, cadaver lab, library, laboratory, 3D Anatomage, hostel rooms, mess hall.

**What the admissions package includes:** MEA and foreign-affairs authentication, apostille of academic documents, visa appointment and preparation, embassy visa interview fee, visa from the Philippines embassy in India, foreign-exchange assistance, one India-Philippines flight ticket, airport pickup and transfer to the hostel, and a Philippines mobile SIM.

Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.

Money

## What to ask the college for

The price difference between DMSF and Cebu is real, so get it itemised rather than quoted as one lump:

1.

### Tuition per year and the programme total

With the academic year printed on the sheet.

2.

### What the anatomy lab access costs

Included in tuition or charged separately. Ask directly.

3.

### Hostel and mess costs, separately

Mess is often the line that changes between the quote and the reality.

4.

### Coaching fees and when they start

Which year, how many hours, and whether attendance is required.

5.

### The refund policy in writing

Particularly if the visa is refused.

6.

### The internship hospital and its NMC compliance

Which hospital, how long, and confirmation of the onsite requirement.

Add the flights. Davao costs more to reach than Cebu, twice a year, for five years. [The full cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md) includes that line.

## Before you pay anyone

Verify, in this order

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

DMSF is also frequently sold with a package that includes hostel and coaching. Ask for each part priced separately so you can see what you are actually buying.

Official website: [dmsf.edu.ph](https://dmsf.edu.ph).

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) for this intake.

title: "Brokenshire College Davao: Fees, Review, NMC Status (2027)"
description: "Brokenshire College in Davao reviewed: small batches, faculty who know your name, a smaller attached hospital, FMGE coaching and a cadaver lab."

Davao City

# Brokenshire College

The quiet option. Smaller batches mean faculty know your name, which matters if you learn by being asked questions. The attached hospital is smaller than DMSF's, and that matters from third year onwards.

Reviewed November 2026. Based on Brokenshire graduates, not first-hand study here.

## The facts

City

Davao City, Davao del Sur

Programme

Doctor of Medicine

Duration

About 5.5 years with internship

Language

English

FMGE coaching

Yes

Official site

[brokenshire.edu.ph](https://brokenshire.edu.ph)

The short version

A good balance of cost and attention. Less crowded than DMSF, so professors are accessible and the queue for practicals is shorter.

What you lose is clinical volume. A smaller hospital means fewer rare cases and fewer deliveries in front of you, and the difference shows in confidence later.

Where this comes from

This page leans on Brokenshire graduates and their notes on the course, not on first-hand study. If something here matters to your money, verify it with the college.

The good

## What works here

- **Small batches.** Faculty learn your name and notice when you are slipping. In a batch of hundreds, nobody notices.

- **A cadaver lab.** Actual dissection, which several students at bigger colleges only get through a screen and a model.

- **Accessible professors.** You can ask a question after class and get an answer, not a form.

- **A quieter environment.** Davao is calmer, the campus is calmer, and there is less to spend money on. For a student who gets distracted, that is a feature.

- **FMGE coaching available.** Not the strongest of the six, but present.

- **Indian mess nearby.** You will not have to cook every day, which is more than JMC can offer.

The trade

## What you give up

- **The attached hospital is smaller.** This is the one to weigh hardest. Fewer patients means fewer cases, and clinical years are where case volume turns into judgement.

- **Fewer Indian students.** A small community is close, but it is also small. If your first year depends on having a group from home, this will be hard.

- **Davao is far from India.** Longer flights, fewer direct options, and an extra connection when something happens at home.

- **Little nightlife or city life.** If you need a city to enjoy, this is not it.

- **Less name recognition.** It is a legitimate college, but it is not a name that opens doors on its own. Nothing in the Philippines really does; your FMGE score does.

Fit

## Who should pick it

A student who learns best in a small room, wants dissection, and does not need a crowd or a city. It also suits a family that wants the college to notice their child.

Not for

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs maximum clinical volume should look at [DMSF](https://drdreams.in/colleges/dmsf.md). Anyone who needs a large Indian community should look at [Perpetual](https://drdreams.in/colleges/perpetual.md). If budget is the constraint, see [Gullas](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md).

Money

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

| Particular | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Enrolment fee | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Book fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | 1,10,000 PHP (Rs 1,59,250) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) |

Fee sheet, Brokenshire College of Medicine, 2026-2027

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, on the Brokenshire and KINGS campus.

- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.

- Refund: the enrolment fee is not refunded.

- Internship: the fee for the one-year internship is discussed at the time of internship.

**Campus facilities:** Classroom, cadaver lab, hospital (Brokenshire Hospital), hostel, laboratory, library.

**What the admissions package includes:** MEA and foreign-affairs authentication, apostille of academic documents, visa appointment and preparation, embassy visa interview fee, visa from the Philippines embassy in India, foreign-exchange assistance, one India-Philippines flight ticket, airport pickup and transfer to the hostel, and a Philippines mobile SIM.

Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.

Money

## What to ask the college for

The appeal here is value with attention, so make sure the quote covers both:

1.

### The current fee sheet

Annual and total, with the academic year on the document.

2.

### Hostel and mess, priced separately

And how far the hostel is from the hospital where you will rotate.

3.

### The batch size for your intake

Ask for a number, not "small". Small is the entire reason to choose this college.

4.

### Which hospital you rotate in, and its bed count

Bed count is a rough proxy for case volume. If the answer is vague, that is information too.

5.

### Refund policy in writing

Before any transfer.

6.

### Internship confirmation for NMC

Which hospital, how long, and that it meets the onsite requirement.

[The cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md) shows how this fits into a five-year total.

## Before you pay anyone

Verify, in this order

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

Small colleges are sometimes described as "easier to get into". Admission is not the bottleneck. Registration in India is.

Official website: [brokenshire.edu.ph](https://brokenshire.edu.ph).

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) for this intake.

Sasa, Davao City

# Jose Maria College

The lowest total cost of the six, and the one with medical missions that put you in front of patients other students only read about. You will cook, live simply, and not have a crowd of countrymen.

Reviewed November 2026. Based on students who studied here, not first-hand study at JMC.

## The facts

City

Sasa, Davao City

Programme

Doctor of Medicine

Duration

About 5.5 years with internship

Language

English

FMGE coaching

Yes

Official site

[jmc.edu.ph](https://jmc.edu.ph)

The short version

If the number is the constraint, this is where the number fits. The medical missions are a genuine educational advantage, not a marketing line.

The infrastructure is basic, the Indian community is tiny, and you will cook most days. Accept those three and the rest is a normal medical course.

Where this comes from

This page comes from students who studied here, and the food complaint has come from every one of them. It is not first-hand study, so weigh the classroom detail accordingly.

The good

## What works here

- **The lowest total cost of the six.** Not the lowest first-year quote. The lowest five-year total, which is the number that matters.

- **Medical missions.** Community health work in barangays, with real patients and limited equipment. It teaches you to examine and decide without a CT scan, which is a skill you will need in India.

- **Small community.** The Indian students who are here tend to be close, because there is no big batch to disappear into.

- **Basic but honest.** Nobody is selling you a luxury campus. What you see is what it is.

- **Often includes documentation help.** Some packages bundle the paperwork and visa guidance. Verify what is actually included, and check whether the price still works once you strip out the extras.

The trade

## What you give up

- **You will cook.** There is no Indian mess culture here. If you arrive unable to make dal and rice, your first month will be miserable and expensive.

- **A very small Indian community.** Fine if you make friends easily. Hard if you were counting on a crowd from home.

- **Basic infrastructure.** Smaller library, older equipment, fewer of the extras. Compare it honestly with Gullas before you decide the saving is worth it.

- **Fewer city amenities.** Sasa is not a student district. Weekends are quiet.

- **The lowest fee attracts its own risk.** Watch for brokers who add a "processing" charge on top of an already low fee. The saving evaporates in one payment.

Fit

## Who should pick it

A highly independent student with a hard budget ceiling, who can cook, who does not need company to function, and who wants community health experience. It suits someone who has already lived away from home.

Not for

## Who should skip it

First-time-away students, anyone who cannot cook, and anyone who needs a big Indian network. If the saving is the only reason you are considering it, check [Gullas](https://drdreams.in/colleges/gcm-gullas.md) first, because the difference may be smaller than you think once food and hostel are counted.

Money

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

| Particular | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Enrolment fee | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Books and uniform fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | 1,20,000 PHP (Rs 1,73,727) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) |

Fee sheet, Jose Maria College Foundation, College of Medicine, 2026-2027

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, at JMCM and the KINGS campus in Chennai.

- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.

- Refund: the enrolment fee is not refunded.

- Internship: the fee for the one-year internship is discussed at the time of internship.

**What the admissions package includes:** MEA and foreign-affairs authentication, apostille of academic documents, visa appointment and preparation, embassy visa interview fee, visa from the Philippines embassy in India, foreign-exchange assistance, one India-Philippines flight ticket, airport pickup and transfer to the hostel, and a Philippines mobile SIM.

Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.

Money

## What to ask the college for

A low fee only saves you money if nothing gets added later:

1.

### The current fee sheet, with the year on it

Annual and total across the programme.

2.

### Exactly what the package includes

Documentation, visa assistance, hostel, mess. Priced separately, so you can see the value of each.

3.

### Hostel cost and kitchen access

If you are cooking, confirm there is a kitchen and what it costs.

4.

### Any local charges payable in pesos

These are usually the ones missing from the quote you get in India.

5.

### Refund policy in writing

Before any transfer, especially for a college sold as a package.

6.

### The internship hospital and NMC compliance

Which hospital, how long, and confirmation of the onsite requirement.

Run the total through the [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost.md), including food you will now be buying and cooking yourself.

## Before you pay anyone

Verify, in this order

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

Low-cost colleges are the ones where a "processing fee" of one lakh appears at the last minute. Ask for the full cost in writing before you commit.

Official website: [jmc.edu.ph](https://jmc.edu.ph).

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) for this intake.

About

# Written by Dr. Nitz

I'm Nitish, and Dr. Nitz is the name I write under. I finished the Doctor of Medicine at Southwestern University in Cebu in 2025. These pages are what I know about studying medicine in the Philippines, written down for the student I was in 2019.

By Dr. Nitz. Last updated 22 November 2026.

## The short version

DrDreams is a set of reference pages about studying medicine in the Philippines, written for Indian students and their parents. It covers recognition, cost, the documents, admission, the exams afterwards, and what the years in between actually feel like.

The information that decides a five-year, twenty-lakh decision is scattered across regulator PDFs, college websites written for a different audience, and group chats where half the answers are wrong. This site puts it in one place, in plain English, with the source for anything that can be checked.

Some of it is first hand. Some comes from classmates, graduates and students I have stayed in touch with. Each page says which, in a line near the top, so you can weigh it.

## The facts

Author

Dr. Nitz (Nitish)

Degree

Doctor of Medicine, Southwestern University, Cebu

Graduated

2025

FMGE

Cleared on the first attempt

Time in the country

Five and a half years in Cebu

Colleges covered

Six, all NMC-listed at the time of writing

Every page

Carries the date it was last reviewed

The author

## One graduate, five and a half years

I landed in Cebu in June 2019 with two suitcases and a folder of documents I had checked four times. The first year was hostel food, a fan that clicked all night, and understanding about two thirds of every lecture. By second year, Cebu was a place I lived in rather than a place I was stuck in.

I finished the MD in 2025 and cleared FMGE on the first attempt. Then I came home to the same question every batch asks: where do I start? Most of these pages are the answer I wish someone had sent me as a PDF.

I am not a professor, a cardiologist or an admissions officer. I am one graduate who kept every fee receipt, read the NMC notices properly, and still remembers what the paperwork felt like at nineteen. Where a page goes beyond that, it says so and links the source.

### On record

| Name | Nitish, writing as Dr. Nitz |
| --- | --- |
| Degree | Doctor of Medicine (MD) |
| College | Southwestern University, Cebu City |
| Graduated | 2025 |
| FMGE | Cleared, first attempt |
| Years in Cebu | Five and a half |

The degree certificate can be sent on request. [Ask here](https://drdreams.in/contact.md).

Method

## How a page gets made

1.

### Start with the primary source

Recognition comes from the [NMC](https://www.nmc.org.in) list and [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). Fees come from the college's own fee sheet for the intake. Exam rules come from NMC and NBEMS notices, not from a coaching centre's summary or a remembered version of the rules. If a claim cannot be traced to one of those, it does not go on the page as fact.

2.

### Say what is wrong with it

Every college page carries cons in the same type as the pros: the size of the Indian batch, the hospital, the hostel, the city, the things graduates complain about when the brochure is closed. A page with no cons is an advertisement, and there are enough of those already.

3.

### Mark what is experience and what is not

Some pages come from five and a half years in Cebu. Others come from graduates and students who studied somewhere I did not. Each one says which, in a line near the top, so you can weigh it. Second-hand detail is useful. Pretending it is first-hand is not.

4.

### Date it, then leave the door open

Rules and fees move. Every page carries the month it was last reviewed, and the review date changes when the content does. Corrections are welcome from anyone, including a college that thinks its page is unfair, and they are checked against the source rather than against who asked loudest.

What these pages do not claim

- That a seat, a visa, an internship or a licence is guaranteed. None of them are.

- That a college is good because it is on the NMC list. The list means recognition, not quality.

- That a fee quoted here will still be the fee when you pay. Fee sheets change every intake, which is why the pages tell you what to ask for.

- That this is medical, legal or immigration advice. It is information from one graduate, and the regulator and the college are the authority.

- Any connection to NMC, NBEMS, CHED, the Philippine government or any college named here.

When a page is wrong, it gets corrected and the correction is dated. That is the whole editorial policy, and the [contact page](https://drdreams.in/contact.md) is how it starts.

Why the site exists

## The account that started it

Everything above is policy. This is the part that explains the policy, and it is the only personal account on the site. It is mine.

"NEET got me a qualification and not a government seat. I applied to Southwestern University in Cebu myself: emailed the admissions office, sent my own documents, and hired a consultant for the embassy paperwork alone. That saved money my family did not have to spare."

"The first year was hard in ways nobody had warned me about. The food, the accent, learning to cook badly. By second year Cebu was a place I lived in rather than a place I was stuck in."

"FMGE I started in second year and did it badly, then got serious in final year. Six to eight hours a day, past papers, a small group I studied with. First attempt."

Dr. Nitz, MD, Southwestern University, Cebu, 2025.

The first year is where most of the questions I get come from, and it is the part no brochure describes. So the site has a page for it, written from the inside rather than from a campus tour. [Life in the Philippines](https://drdreams.in/student-life.md) is the honest version, including the parts that were bad.

Studied in the Philippines?

If you have and want your account on this site, send it. Say whether it can carry your first name, your college and your year. Nothing is edited into praise: the complaints are the useful part.

Student life

## Cebu, on ordinary days

Not a campus brochure. This is what the weekends look like between exam blocks, and it is the same city on a Tuesday. If you are deciding whether to spend five years somewhere, that is the thing worth seeing.

The main page covers the whole route in one sitting: recognition, cost, the entrance problem, and the exams at the end. Everything else on the site hangs off it.

The boundary

## What this is not

### What you get here

- Pages you can read without paying anything

- A source for the claims that matter

- A correction when something is wrong

- An answer to a question the pages do not cover

### What you will not get

- Anyone to file your application for you

- Documents held, checked or forwarded on your behalf

- Money moved, a seat reserved or a visa guaranteed

- Anything at all for sale

If you want someone to handle the filing, hire a licensed visa consultant and ask for their registration number first. That is a real service with a real price, and it is not this site. What this site can do is make sure you know which documents to gather, what the visa actually requires, and what a college should be putting in writing before you pay it.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/documents-required.md) is the page to read before you sign anything.

## Read this before you write

Most questions that arrive are answered already, usually on the guide or the costs page. It is faster than waiting for a reply, and it is the version with the sources attached.

Legal

# Privacy

Short version: the enquiry form does not store anything on a server. It opens WhatsApp with your message. Here is everything else.

Last updated 22 November 2026.

## What is collected

Nothing is collected automatically beyond what any web server logs: the pages you request, your approximate location from your IP address, and your browser type. Those logs exist at the hosting provider and are used for security and to see which pages people read.

## The message form

The form on the [contact page](https://drdreams.in/contact.md) is not connected to a database. When you press send, your browser opens WhatsApp with a message already written. Nothing is transmitted to this site or stored on it.

Once the message reaches WhatsApp, it is handled under WhatsApp's own privacy terms, not ours. We see your name, your number and whatever you typed. That conversation is kept for as long as it is useful to your plans, and you are not added to a mailing list.

## What we do not do

- We do not sell, rent or share your details with colleges, recruiters or advertisers.

- We do not run a newsletter, so there is nothing to unsubscribe from.

- We do not ask for original documents through this site.

## Cookies and local storage

The site stores one thing in your browser: your light or dark theme choice, kept in local storage. It never leaves your device and you can clear it from your browser settings at any time.

There are no tracking cookies set by the site itself.

## Other services this site loads

- **Google Fonts**, for the typefaces. Google receives your IP address when the font loads.

- **The hosting provider**, which keeps standard access logs.

- **Advertising**, if ads are shown on a page, the ad network may set its own cookies under its own policy. You can control those through your browser or the network's ad settings.

## Your choices

You can ask for the WhatsApp or email conversation to be deleted at any point, and it will be. If you want to know what is held about you, ask. The answer will be whatever is in our chat and nothing more.

## Contact

Email drnitz@proton.me for anything to do with this policy. Privacy questions get the same treatment as everything else: a reply from me, usually within a couple of days.

## Changes

If this policy changes, the date at the top changes with it. There is no version history to dig through because there is nothing here worth hiding.

Legal

# Disclaimer

This site is one doctor's experience and reading of the rules, offered in good faith. It is not a regulator, a college, or a guarantee.

Last updated 22 November 2026.

## Who writes this

DrDreams is written by a graduate of the Doctor of Medicine programme at Southwestern University in Cebu. It is a reference site about studying medicine in the Philippines, aimed at Indian students and their families.

The site is not affiliated with the National Medical Commission, NBEMS, the Philippine government or any college named on these pages. College names and links are there to describe the institutions, not to imply a partnership with them.

## Information changes

Fees, intake dates, curricula and NMC requirements change, sometimes with little notice. Every page here carries a review date. Where rules matter to your money or your registration, check the primary source first: the [NMC](https://www.nmc.org.in), [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org), and the college's own admissions office.

Nothing on this site overrides a written communication from the college or a notice from the regulator.

## No guarantee

DrDreams cannot and does not guarantee admission, a visa, an internship placement, an FMGE or NExT result, or registration with any medical council. Anyone who promises any of those outcomes in advance is overstating what any website can know.

## Opinions, not rankings

The ratings and the "best for" notes are subjective judgements from five and a half years in the Philippines, plus what graduates and students reported. They are not an official ranking and they are not a measurement of teaching quality. Where the page is not first hand, it says so.

## Not medical or legal advice

This site gives educational guidance about studying abroad. It is not medical advice, legal advice or immigration advice. For visa and immigration questions, use a licensed professional or the Philippine embassy in your country. For medical questions, see a doctor.

## What this site is

These pages explain how studying medicine in the Philippines works: the degree and how long it takes, the colleges and their recognition, the documents, the costs, the exams afterwards and the life around them. They are written to be read before money is committed, and each one carries the month it was last reviewed.

## External links

Links to colleges, regulators and resources are there so you can check the claims. We do not control those sites and are not responsible for their content or their accuracy.

## Errors

If something here is wrong, tell us at drnitz@proton.me and it will be corrected, with the review date changed on the page. That offer is genuine: a wrong fee on this site costs a family more than it costs the person who wrote it.
